title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: Unlike iron and cobalt clusters, which deflect only toward the strong field and fit superparamagnetism, gadolinium, terbium, and dysprosium clusters show two size-dependent Stern-Gerlach responses: a sharp superparamagnetic profile or a broad locked-moment profile.
review_scope: Neutral Gd, Tb, and Dy clusters in gradient-magnet deflection experiments; Fe and Co clusters only as the contrasting superparamagnetic case.
review_conditions: Laser-vaporization beam, collimation, Stern-Gerlach deflection, then excimer ionization and time-of-flight detection. Superparamagnetic at all studied temperatures: Gd22, Tb17, Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, and Dy27.
review_caveats: Dysprosium results are described as preliminary. Which model applies is size specific, not a single rare-earth rule.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: For superparamagnetic rare-earth clusters, vibrational temperature can be taken as the source temperature once deflection saturates with increasing source residence time, indicating thermal equilibrium with the source.
review_scope: Superparamagnetic rare-earth clusters produced in the laser-vaporization source and measured by Stern-Gerlach deflection.
review_conditions: Residence time set by the beam chopper; source temperatures reported in Table 1 span about 73-303 K.
review_caveats: This equates vibrational temperature with source temperature only after saturation. Rotational temperature is separately cooled by the expansion and is not equal to the source temperature.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: Among clusters that remain superparamagnetic at all studied temperatures, Tb17 has an internal moment per atom that is independent of temperature, whereas Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, Dy27, and Gd22 have internal moments per atom that increase with vibrational temperature.
review_scope: Gd22, Tb17, Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, and Dy27 in the superparamagnetic regime.
review_conditions: Vibrational temperatures about 73-303 K; low-field Langevin approximation μ_eff ≈ N μ^2 B / 3kT when NμB/kT ≪ 1, with the full Langevin form used for the reported internal moments.
review_caveats: The antiferromagnetic interpretation is proposed, not demonstrated. Some Table 1 entries are missing or have large uncertainties, especially Dy at high temperature.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: Clusters that are not purely superparamagnetic are described by a moment rigidly locked to the lattice, so the trajectory depends on initial rotational conditions; supersonic expansion cools rotation strongly while leaving vibration at the source temperature.
review_scope: Locked-moment rare-earth clusters, illustrated for Tb23 and stated for the remaining non-superparamagnetic sizes; rotational cooling is a general feature of the supersonic beam.
review_conditions: Example profile at 98 K, B = 0.267 T, dB/dz = 101.3 T/m. Fit parameters are rotational temperature, magnetic moment, and superparamagnetic fraction.
review_caveats: The 4 K rotational temperature and 10-20% superparamagnetic fraction are fit results for the Tb23 profile, not universal constants. The model assumes adiabatic entry and a statistical distribution of initial conditions.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: Locked-moment Gd and Tb clusters have internal moments per atom far below the bulk atomic moments, and those moments increase with applied field and with decreasing temperature.
review_scope: Locked-moment gadolinium and terbium clusters; the below-bulk statement in the conclusions covers the rare-earth clusters in this study.
review_conditions: Moments extracted from Stern-Gerlach profiles under the locked-moment model as field and temperature are varied.
review_caveats: Ranges are across sizes and conditions, not a single moment for every size. Dysprosium locked-moment moments are not given as a comparable range. Superparamagnetic moments are also below bulk but follow different temperature trends.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: Some sizes that are locked-moment at low vibrational temperature unlock toward superparamagnetism as temperature rises, passing through an intermediate regime in which the moment can explore a solid angle between the locked and free limits.
review_scope: Selected Gd and Tb cluster sizes that are locked at low temperature, especially Tb26 and Gd17, and also Tb21 and Tb25.
review_conditions: Increasing vibrational temperature; Fig. 2 compares Tb26 with Tb17 and Tb23 at higher fields as temperature increases (about 0.267 T, 0.540 T, and 0.673 T). Intermediate behavior is illustrated for Tb26 at 198 K.
review_caveats: Not all locked sizes are reported to unlock in the studied range. Intermediate profiles are a qualitative mismatch to both models, not a third fitted Hamiltonian.

title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
review_claim: A single attached oxygen atom does not account for the two magnetic behaviors of rare-earth clusters: above about 200 K, Tb_n and Tb_nO generally have the same deflection behavior, with only specific low-temperature exceptions.
review_scope: Terbium clusters with one oxygen atom, n < 40, compared with the corresponding clean clusters.
review_conditions: Low-temperature differences are reported for Tb21O and Tb25O; Tb21 and Tb21O match by 198 K, and Tb25 and Tb25O match above 248 K. Fig. 3 fields are 0.267 T at 98 K, 0.405 T at 148 K, and 0.540 T at 198 K.
review_caveats: The authors' statement that oxygen has little effect is explicitly qualified by these low-temperature exceptions. The unlocking and partial-locking roles of oxygen are size specific and not a general oxygen effect.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Ligand-controlled hydrolysis, using peripheral polydentate ligands to limit lanthanide hydrolysis and stabilize discrete hydroxo species, is the established route to polynuclear lanthanide clusters, but without anion templates it mainly yields low-nuclearity species (typically fewer than 20 metal ions).
review_scope: Homometallic lanthanide hydroxide clusters assembled under ligand-controlled hydrolysis.
review_conditions: Outcome depends on metal-ion source, metal/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and reaction duration; early tetranuclear amino-acid examples were isolated near pH 6–7 rather than the previously used pH 4.
review_caveats: The <20 nuclearity statement is the authors’ generalization over the ligand families they list, not a strict physical limit.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Rational design of lanthanide clusters remains difficult because the product is highly sensitive to the starting materials and to metal/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and time; the authors therefore prioritize assembly-mechanism studies and, separately, structure–property work that this review does not cover.
review_scope: Synthetic lanthanide-cluster chemistry as framed by this review, especially high-nuclearity hydroxide clusters.
review_conditions: Sensitive variables named by the authors: metal ion/ligand ratio, pH, solvent, temperature and duration, plus identity of the starting materials.
review_caveats: Structure–property relationships, including SMM and magnetocaloric behavior mentioned only as motivation in the introduction, are explicitly outside the review’s analysis.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Small anions are needed to grow higher-nuclearity lanthanide clusters, and slow release of anions, multiple anions, or mixed anions templates assembly more effectively than a single anion because they disperse concentrated positive charge while also balancing charge.
review_scope: High-nuclearity lanthanide hydroxide clusters using halide or oxoanion templates.
review_conditions: Slow release is achieved by in situ ligand or solvent decomposition, often under hydro/solvothermal conditions, or by absorption of atmospheric CO2 at a suitable pH.
review_caveats: The advantage over a single-anion template is a comparative claim based on the surveyed clusters (Table 1), not a quantitative ranking of template strength.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Direct addition of carbonate salts can template lanthanide clusters but is generally discouraged at atmospheric pressure; slow in situ generation of carbonate, or CO2 fixation under controlled pH, is preferred so that carbonate precipitation does not outrun hydrolysis and cluster assembly.
review_scope: Carbonate-templated lanthanide clusters, especially giant cages and wheels.
review_conditions: Ln24 examples: isonicotinic acid, CuO and Ln(NO3)3·6H2O in DMF at 160 °C. Air-derived carbonate examples include methanol (La7), mixed EtOH–CH3CN (Ln37), and ligand systems that fix CO2 without added carbonate salts.
review_caveats: Direct carbonate addition is shown to work for the chiral Ln14 pair, so the warning is a practical tendency, not an absolute prohibition.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Mixed anion templates can act cooperatively: strongly coordinating oxoanions build the hydroxo units, while encapsulated halide or perchlorate ions disperse and balance excess positive charge, and changing the anion set can switch the resulting architecture.
review_scope: Giant lanthanide hydroxide cages and barrels (about Ln27–Ln48) using mixed halide/oxoanion templates.
review_conditions: Gd38/Gd48 are CAA-supported clusters; Er48 and Ln36 are hydrothermal nicotinate assemblies; Ho48 is hydrothermal from Ho2O3, Mn(OAc)2, isonicotinic acid, formic acid and KBr, with carbonate ascribed to oxidation of formic acid.
review_caveats: For spherical Ln36 the prose assigns six nitrates to the {Ln24} wheel and two chlorides to the cavity, while the Fig. 12 caption emphasizes six nitrates; template roles should be read with that internal inconsistency.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Multiple copies of the same oxoanion, not only mixed anion types, can stitch many small hydroxo motifs into giant cages or tubes, with the anions both templating faces or wheels and supporting the skeleton.
review_scope: Highest-nuclearity lanthanide-exclusive clusters surveyed (Er60, Dy72, Ln104).
review_conditions: Er60: controlled hydrolysis of Er(ClO4)3 with L-threonine. Ln104: hydrolysis of Ln(ClO4)3 with Co(CH3COO)2·4H2O and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. Dy72: mda/mdaH ligands with nitrate.
review_caveats: Ln104 is described as the highest-nuclearity lanthanide-exclusive clusters reported at the time of the review; that ranking is time-bound.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: High-nuclearity lanthanide hydroxide clusters are assembled from a small set of recurring polyhedra—triangular {Ln3(μ3-OH)}, cubane {Ln4(μ3-OH)4}, trigonal-bipyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, square-pyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)} and octahedral {Ln6(μ6-O)(μ3-OH)8}—by vertex-, edge- or face-sharing, often of more than one motif.
review_scope: Lanthanide hydroxide cluster cores from small oligomers through Ln104, including some heterometallic examples such as Zn4@Ln24.
review_caveats: Some figure captions use the word square pyramid for {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, whereas the text and Fig. 16 assign that formula to the trigonal bipyramid and {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)} to the square pyramid; the textual assignment is the consistent one.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: The cubane {Ln4(μ3-OH)4} is the most common single building block; vertex-sharing cubanes produce Ln7, wheel-like Ln12 and Ln15, and cage-like Ln38 and Ln60, and the higher-nuclearity members of this series characteristically contain template anions whereas the lower-nuclearity ones do not.
review_scope: Clusters whose cores are described as built only from cubanes or only from triangular {Ln3(μ3-OH)} units.
review_caveats: The nuclearity–template correlation is observational across the cited series, not a proof that a template is always required above a fixed nuclearity.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Clusters generated from only trigonal-bipyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, only square-pyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)}, or only octahedral {Ln6(μ6-O)(μ3-OH)8} units are rare compared with triangle- and cubane-based families.
review_scope: Lanthanide clusters whose cores are assigned to a single one of these three motifs.
review_caveats: Rarity is relative to the literature covered through 2017 and to the authors’ structural classification; Ln104 shows that the square-pyramidal motif can still reach very high nuclearity when templated.

title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
review_claim: Vertex-sharing of mixed hydroxo building blocks is a general way to increase structural diversity, and the clusters above nuclearity 20 that are drawn from these mixed-motif families are typically supported by template anions.
review_scope: Lanthanide hydroxide clusters assembled from two different basic polyhedra.
review_caveats: Some lower-nuclearity mixed-motif clusters (Ln11–Ln19, Ln14) are listed alongside the templated giants, so mixed building blocks alone do not guarantee nuclearity above 20.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Bright Ln3+ emission with quantum yields above about 50% generally requires ligand antenna sensitization rather than direct 4f–4f excitation, with the ligand–metal energy gap matched to the target ion and high-energy oscillators kept out of the coordination sphere.
review_scope: Molecular Ln3+ complexes intended as luminescent materials, including luminescent SMMs.
review_conditions: Indirect excitation through ligand chromophores; suppression of non-radiative paths from inner- and outer-sphere OH, NH, and CH oscillators.
review_caveats: Direct f–f excitation remains possible but rarely gives highly luminescent materials. A direct singlet-to-Ln energy transfer is described as much less probable than the singlet–triplet–Ln route.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Across the compiled Dy3+ examples the magnetic effective barrier is usually lower than the first-excited-state gap measured by luminescence, showing that dynamic magnetometry underestimates the crystal-field gap when extra relaxation channels operate.
review_scope: Dy3+ luminescent SMMs for which both magnetic Δ and spectroscopic Δ_Orbach are reported.
review_conditions: Comparison of ac magnetometry with emission-derived crystal-field gaps.
review_caveats: Not every entry follows the inequality; inequivalent sites can also occur in mononuclear complexes and undermine a single-gap comparison.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Ln3+ luminescence is fixed mainly by the first coordination shell, but ion–ion interactions in extended solids can partially quench emission and change lifetimes, so dimensionality can affect optics even when slow relaxation remains single-ion.
review_scope: Extended Dy3+ coordination polymers that show single-ion slow relaxation and Ln luminescence.
review_conditions: Systems in which magnetic relaxation is of single-ion origin.
review_caveats: The influence of dimensionality on emission is proposed, not demonstrated by a completed comparative study.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Yb3+ luminescent SMMs are harder to realize than Dy3+ analogues because the smaller J lowers doublet axiality, and a large mismatch between the magnetic barrier and the luminescence gap means under-barrier processes dominate.
review_scope: Yb3+ complexes with beta-diketonate/tetrathiafulvalene or tripodal Schiff-base ligands.
review_conditions: Field-induced or weakly blocked Yb3+ SMMs; crystal-field gaps from luminescence, sometimes with EPR and calculations.
review_caveats: Some related Yb complexes are not SMMs because the ground state is not pure Ising. The very large spectroscopic gaps are not realized as magnetic barriers in the cited systems.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Luminescent Er3+ SMMs are scarce because prolate Er3+ needs an equatorial field, often from organometallic ligands, and NIR emission is readily quenched by O–H, C–H, and C–N oscillators.
review_scope: Er3+ SMMs, especially NIR-emissive coordination and organometallic complexes.
review_conditions: Equatorial crystal field for anisotropy; NIR excitation or antenna sensitization when non-radiative oscillators are controlled.
review_caveats: The good magnetic–optical agreement is a single cited example, not a broad series.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Tb3+ luminescent SMMs need high symmetry to slow the magnetization, and their luminescence-derived gaps are often much larger than the modest magnetic barriers, whereas Tb3+ emission is easier to sensitize and resolve at room temperature than Dy3+ emission.
review_scope: Tb3+ luminescent SMMs, mainly Zn/Tb Schiff-base and related coordination complexes.
review_conditions: High-symmetry axial coordination; emission analysis of 5D4 → 7F6.
review_caveats: Reported magnetic barriers in the bifunctional Tb examples are modest, and slow relaxation still requires precise coordination control.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Nd3+ and Ho3+ are underused for luminescent SMMs: Nd3+ barriers stay small because low axiality is hard to impose on early lanthanides, and Ho3+ suffers strong QTM from its non-Kramers character and I = 7/2 hyperfine coupling, with no luminescent Ho3+ SMM known to the authors.
review_scope: Nd3+, Ho3+, and Ce3+ molecular magnets considered as potential luminescent SMMs.
review_caveats: Absence of Ho3+ luminescent SMMs is the authors’ knowledge claim at the time of the review, not a physical prohibition.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: An applied magnetic field can Zeeman-split or shift Ln3+ emission lines of SMMs, providing an independent check of the lowest mJ gaps, but intensity changes are expected to be weak because the magnetic field has even parity under Judd–Ofelt selection rules.
review_scope: Luminescent Dy3+ SMMs studied under static or pulsed magnetic fields.
review_conditions: Low temperature (example at 5 K) and high pulsed fields (up to 36 T in the cited Cs–Dy study).
review_caveats: Field-dependent spectra may not resolve every zero-field component. True synergy with superparamagnetic coercivity below the blocking temperature had not been shown.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: A genuine synergy in which SMM coercivity below the blocking temperature modifies the emission has not been established, because most luminescent SMMs have low barriers and weak remanence; ligands must still be designed to be both strongly axial and efficient sensitizers, with blocking above about 10 K.
review_scope: Luminescent Ln3+ SMMs aimed at magnetic-field-tunable emission.
review_conditions: Blocking temperature high enough (stated as >10 K) to track temperature-dependent changes, plus sustainable remanence.
review_caveats: This is an outlook and a stated experimental gap, not a measured cross-effect.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Chiral or polar luminescent Ln SMMs can add NCD, SHG, piezo/pyroelectricity, magneto-chiral dichroism, magnetization-induced second-harmonic generation, and circularly polarized luminescence, and crystallization in a polar group can add ferroelectricity.
review_scope: Chiral or polar multifunctional Ln SMMs, including the enantiopure Zn2+/Dy3+ Schiff-base ferroelectric.
review_conditions: Non-centrosymmetric or polar crystal structures, often from chiral ligands.
review_caveats: Most cross-effects (MChD, MSHG, magneto-electric coupling) are presented as opportunities rather than results demonstrated across the family. The record electrical-hysteresis temperature is one cited molecular example.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Eu3+ emission is a particularly useful local-structure probe: Stark-component counts, relative intensities, line energies, and decay curves report site multiplicity, coordinated water, local symmetry, ligand-field magnitude, covalency, and nearby vibrations.
review_scope: Ln3+ complexes, especially Eu3+ as a spectroscopic probe of the local coordination sphere.
review_conditions: Analysis of intra-4f manifolds, including excitation-wavelength and temperature dependence and decay curves.
review_caveats: The section presents this as a general spectroscopic capability, not as a demonstrated SMM design rule for Eu3+ itself.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: In Ln3+ SMMs the spin–orbit coupling greatly exceeds the crystal-field splitting, so single-ion anisotropy of the crystal-field mJ states, rather than a strongly exchange-coupled multilevel spin, sets the anisotropy barrier.
review_scope: Lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets.
review_conditions: Strong spin–orbit coupling, stated as one to two orders of magnitude larger than the crystal-field splitting.
review_caveats: Polynuclear dipolar or exchange interactions can still modify relaxation even when single-ion anisotropy dominates.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Oblate 4f density (for example Nd3+, Tb3+, Dy3+) is stabilized by an axial crystal field, whereas prolate density (for example Er3+) is stabilized by an equatorial field; the preferred geometry therefore follows the mJ electron-density shape.
review_scope: Ln3+ SMMs designed by crystal-field electrostatics.
review_conditions: Ligand geometry chosen to match the ground (and relevant excited) mJ density.
review_caveats: The simple oblate/prolate assignment is not universal for every mJ level of a given ion, as illustrated for Yb3+.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Quantum tunnelling of the magnetization in Ln3+ SMMs is reduced by enforcing high local symmetry, particularly square-antiprismatic D4d, pentagonal-bipyramidal D5h, or linear D∞h coordination.
review_scope: Ln3+ SMMs, including non-Kramers Tb3+ systems.
review_conditions: Accurate control of the lanthanide coordination geometry.
review_caveats: High symmetry is necessary but not sufficient; Raman and direct processes, and interactions in polynuclear compounds, can still limit blocking.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: When the ground-to-first-excited gap is large and QTM and Raman paths are suppressed, relaxation is mainly Orbach; relaxation through higher doublets (thermally activated QTM) requires strong axiality of both the ground and excited states and can produce barriers of hundreds to more than a thousand kelvin.
review_scope: Relaxation dynamics of genuine high-barrier Ln3+ SMMs.
review_conditions: Large crystal-field gap and shortcut of Raman and ground-state QTM; strong axiality of excited doublets for high-lying TA-QTM.
review_caveats: The temperature dependence is generally a mixture of processes, so a single Arrhenius barrier can misrepresent the mechanism.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Dipolar interactions generally enhance QTM by generating a transverse field, whereas exchange can either suppress tunnelling, as in strongly coupled radical-bridged dimers, or enhance it when inequivalent lanthanide sites create a local transverse field.
review_scope: Polynuclear and polyheteronuclear Ln3+ SMMs.
review_conditions: Presence of dipolar and/or exchange coupling between spin carriers.
review_caveats: The authors explicitly say the situation is not fully understood and generalization is difficult.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: Bifunctional luminescent SMMs are most often built from Kramers ions Dy3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ (and less often Nd3+ and Ho3+), with Dy3+ and Tb3+ as visible emitters and Nd3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ as NIR emitters; ligands must simultaneously impose the anisotropy-producing geometry and sensitize the ion.
review_scope: Design of molecular luminescent Ln3+ SMMs.
review_conditions: Organic ligands or ancillary complexes that both shape the coordination sphere and act as antennas.
review_caveats: Adding luminescence makes optimization harder because the same ligands must satisfy magnetic and optical criteria.

title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
review_claim: High-resolution Ln3+ luminescence gives the crystal-field (Orbach) gap that can be compared with the magnetic activation energy, so agreement indicates dominant Orbach relaxation while a smaller magnetic barrier indicates under-barrier QTM, Raman, or direct processes, and a larger magnetic barrier indicates relaxation via higher doublets.
review_scope: Luminescent Ln3+ SMMs, chiefly mononuclear Dy3+, with extensions to Yb3+, Er3+, and Tb3+.
review_conditions: Resolved emission, often at low temperature for Dy3+; comparison of ac-derived Δ with the spectroscopic ground-to-excited gap.
review_caveats: The correlation has mainly been done on mononuclear species. Crystallographically inequivalent sites, hot bands, and vibronic lines complicate the assignment; EPR, INS, MCD, and calculations are recommended to confirm the splitting.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Atomically precise polynuclear metal clusters are useful model catalysts for water splitting and CO2 conversion because their defined structures allow structure–property analysis and because multiple metal centers can act cooperatively in multielectron reactions.
review_scope: Polynuclear metal clusters, especially lanthanide-only and lanthanide–transition-metal clusters used for HER, OER, and CO2 conversion.
review_caveats: This is a framing argument; the review does not claim every polynuclear cluster is more active than the corresponding mononuclear complex.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Anchoring a bio-inspired LnCo3 oxygen-evolution cluster to P-doped g-C3N4 through a Co–P linkage lets the cluster accept photogenerated holes, while Ln3+ stabilizes anionic intermediates and the cobalt centers share the oxidative load.
review_scope: LnCo3 clusters covalently supported on phospho-doped graphitic carbon nitride for overall water splitting.
review_conditions: UV–vis irradiation, λ > 300 nm, pure water; stoichiometric H2:O2 near 2:1.
review_caveats: Activity is loading-dependent; 1.05 wt% NdCo3/PCN is the reported optimum, not every loading.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Introducing Zr or Ti into Ce6-node UiO-66 increases the driving force for ligand-to-metal charge transfer, narrows the gap, and experimentally gives mixed-metal frameworks higher overall-water-splitting activity and lower recombination than single-metal analogues.
review_scope: Ce6-based UiO-66 and mixed Zr/Ce/Ti UiO-66 photocatalysts for overall water splitting.
review_conditions: Xe-lamp UV–vis or visible irradiation in water; repeated use without an obvious activity drop was reported for the trimetallic MOF.
review_caveats: Transient-absorption inactivation curves of the five UiO-66 samples were similar, so the activity difference is not attributed to that particular kinetic observable.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: In the giant Ni36Gd102 cluster, Ni is the CO2-binding site and μ3-OH− can supply protons for C–O cleavage, while Gd3+ is not the direct catalytic center but stabilizes the cluster and tunes the Ni2+ electronic structure and selectivity.
review_scope: High-nuclearity Ni–Gd coordination clusters for visible-light CO2-to-CO reduction.
review_conditions: λ > 420 nm, [Ru(phen)3](PF6)2, TEOA, CH3CN, 0.1 MPa, 1 h.
review_caveats: The Ln role is described for this cluster’s proposed cycle; it does not mean lanthanides are never the redox site in other LnCC CO2-reduction catalysts.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: A porous Eu2 cluster MOF with Ru(phen)3-type ligands selectively photoreduces CO2 to formate through ligand-to-cluster electron transfer and a two-electron Eu(II)–H2–Eu(II) active site.
review_scope: Heterogeneous Eu–Ru(phen)3 MOFs for visible-light CO2 reduction to HCOO−.
review_conditions: λ > 420 nm, TEOA, 0.1 MPa, 10 h.
review_caveats: The review later notes that LnCC photoreduction products demonstrated so far remain the two-electron products CO and HCOOH.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Partial replacement of Zr4+ by Ce4+ in Cu/UiO-66 does not raise the methanol yield from CO2 hydrogenation but can increase methanol selectivity; oxygen spillover between Ce4+ and Cu0 is invoked to explain a loss of Cu0 sites and a lower yield than Cu/UiO-66(Zr).
review_scope: Cu-loaded mixed Ce/Zr UiO-66 for thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.
review_conditions: 200 °C, 1.8 MPa, H2/CO2 = 3:1, 25 h; reported yield 397 μmolMeOH gCu−1 h−1 and 56% selectivity.
review_caveats: The oxygen-spillover explanation is the review’s reading of that study and is specific to Cu on Ce/Zr nodes.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Bis(amidinate) lanthanide amide dimers catalyze carboxylation of terminal alkynes with CO2 at ambient pressure through alkyne aminolysis to a metal acetylide, CO2 insertion into the Ln–C bond, and transmetalation with Cs2CO3.
review_scope: Dinuclear organolanthanide amide clusters for C–C bond formation between terminal alkynes and CO2.
review_conditions: Cs2CO3, 40 °C, 0.1 MPa, 24 h for the Nd2 entry.
review_caveats: A stoichiometric acid quench is required to release the carboxylic acid from the cesium carboxylate. Related Gd–Cu MOFs operate at 80 °C rather than 40 °C.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Lanthanide complexes can construct C–N bonds from CO2 and 2-aminobenzonitriles or aziridines under milder conditions than many transition-metal systems because their metal–ligand interactions are weakly covalent, labile, and nondirectional, allowing substrates to approach from multiple directions.
review_scope: Amidato dinuclear Eu and Yb clusters for CO2 cycloaddition to 2-aminobenzonitriles or aziridines.
review_conditions: Eu2a: DBU, 100 °C, 0.1 MPa, 24 h, 91% yield; Eu2b: DBU, 50 °C, 0.1 MPa, 48 h, 90% yield.
review_caveats: The directional-approach argument is a general lanthanide bonding rationale illustrated by these clusters, not a quantified comparison across all transition-metal catalysts.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: LnCC-catalyzed cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides follows Lewis-acid activation of the epoxide oxygen, nucleophilic ring opening, CO2 capture by the opened alkoxide, and ring closure to the cyclic carbonate.
review_scope: Lanthanide and 3d–4f cluster catalysts, usually with a bromide nucleophile such as TBAB, for cyclic-carbonate synthesis.
review_conditions: Typically TBAB cocatalyst; pressures from 0.1 to 1 MPa and temperatures from 25 to 120 °C depending on the cluster.
review_caveats: A nucleophilic cocatalyst is part of the stated mechanism; activity without TBAB is not established by this summary.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: For CO2/epoxide cycloaddition, close Ln and Zn centers often give a synergistic rate enhancement over mononuclear lanthanide complexes, but a crowded heterometallic coordination sphere can instead lower activity relative to a less hindered homometallic analogue.
review_scope: Homo- and heterometallic Ln and Ln–Zn clusters for cyclic-carbonate synthesis.
review_conditions: TBAB is the usual cocatalyst; the record TOFs are at 120 °C and 1 MPa for 1 h.
review_caveats: Whether heterometallic synergy helps depends on ligand crowding and substrate substitution; it is not uniform across the cited families.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Among isostructural trinuclear Ln3-MOFs, cycloaddition activity increases as the lanthanide radius decreases in the order Y > Er > Tb.
review_scope: Trinuclear lanthanide-cluster MOFs with BDC or NDC linkers for CO2/epoxide cycloaddition.
review_conditions: 60 °C, 1 MPa CO2, 12 h; Y3–BDC TON 543 in Table 3.
review_caveats: The radius–activity correlation is for these isomorphic series, not a general ranking of all LnCC carbonate catalysts.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: In lanthanide-functionalized [SiW11O39] clusters, redox-inactive Ln3+ can raise photocatalytic HER activity relative to the parent polyoxotungstate, an effect attributed to Lewis acidity rather than Ln-centered redox.
review_scope: Ln-functionalized Keggin-derived polyoxotungstates Ln[(pdc)2Ln(H2O)2SiW11O39] for HER.
review_conditions: Photocatalysis with 470 nm irradiation, [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2, ascorbic acid, and H2O/MeOH (9:1); LaW11 TON 525 and TOF 324 h−1 in Table 1.
review_caveats: The Lewis-acidity/PCET interpretation is proposed because the chosen Ln ions are redox inactive; it is not a direct spectroscopic proof of the proton-transfer step.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Heterometallic Ln–Zn and Ln–Co complexes copolymerize CO2 and cyclohexene oxide by chain shuttling: Lewis-acidic Ln binds the epoxide, a labile Zn- or Co-bound acetate/carbonate opens the ring, and the resulting Ln-alkoxide inserts into Zn-bound CO2 to grow the polycarbonate.
review_scope: Heterometallic Ln–Zn/Co complexes, including macrocyclic tris(salen) and hexoxime systems, for alternating CO2/cyclohexene oxide copolymerization.
review_conditions: Varies widely, for example Nd2Zn at 70 °C and 0.7 MPa, and NdCo3 at 130 °C and 2 MPa.
review_caveats: High carbonate selectivity does not imply a narrow PDI; several homometallic and Y4Zn2 entries have PDIs from about 2 to 9.8. One ligand family that is less active for cycloaddition can still copolymerize.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Synergistic effects in multimetallic LnCCs are repeatedly inferred but still need direct verification, electrocatalytic HER and CO2 reduction with LnCCs remain essentially undeveloped, and demonstrated LnCC photoreduction products are limited to CO and formic acid.
review_scope: The reviewed LnCC catalysts for water splitting and CO2 conversion as of this 2022 survey.
review_caveats: Electrocatalytic OER examples are discussed earlier, so the electrocatalysis gap is specifically HER and CO2 reduction, not all electrocatalysis.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Homogeneous LnCC HER catalysts are limited by a narrow photoresponse and difficult recovery, whereas anchoring atomically precise Ln–transition-metal clusters on a semiconductor can improve charge separation, supply HER sites, and ease recycling.
review_scope: Supported Ln52Ni56−xCdx/CdS composites versus homogeneous LnCC photocatalysts.
review_conditions: Visible light, λ > 420 nm, Na2S/Na2SO3 in water.
review_caveats: The high rate is specific to the Eu composite; Pr, Nd, and Gd analogues do not open the same second electron-transfer path.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: On CdS, a variable-valence Eu center enables a second charge-transfer channel in addition to transfer into the cluster LUMO, whereas Pr, Nd, and Gd do not because the CdS conduction band lies positive of their Ln3+/Ln2+ potentials.
review_scope: Ln52Ni56−xCdx/CdS photocatalytic HER, comparing Eu with Pr, Nd, and Gd.
review_conditions: Visible-light irradiation, λ > 420 nm.
review_caveats: The argument depends on the relative positions of the CdS band edge and the Ln3+/Ln2+ couples; it should not be generalized to other semiconductors without those alignments.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Photosensitizer-modified Ce6 metal–organic layers drive HER by a dual excitation sequence in which the reduced Ru or Ir ligand reduces Ce(IV) to Ce(III), and spin-allowed 4f→5d excitation of Ce(III) then reduces protons.
review_scope: Ce6(μ3-O)4(μ3-OH)4 cluster MOLs with Ru or Ir photosensitizing ligands.
review_conditions: UV–vis 350–700 nm; BIH; MeCN:AcOH (40:1); Ce6–BTB–Ir TON 1357 in Table 1.
review_caveats: The dual-path mechanism is reported for these Ce(IV/III) MOLs and is not claimed for redox-inert lanthanides.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Electrocatalytic HER with LnCCs is rarely reported because the clusters generally have poor conductivity and are unstable under electrocatalytic conditions.
review_scope: LnCC electrocatalysts for HER.
review_caveats: LnW11 is an exception that was also tested electrocatalytically; the limitation is stated as the prevailing situation, not an absolute absence of examples.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Replacing one Co2+ of a Co4 cubane water-oxidation catalyst by a redox-inert Ln3+ gives an LnCo3 cubane that both mimics the Ca site of the natural OEC and uses flexible water/acetate ligands to improve photocatalytic water oxidation.
review_scope: 3d–4f cubane [LnCo3(hmp)(OAc)] water-oxidation catalysts derived from the Co4 hmp cubane.
review_conditions: 470 nm irradiation, [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2, Na2S2O8, water; ErCo3 is the Table 1 entry.
review_caveats: Mn cubanes inspired by {CaMn4O5} are described as often unstable, which is why Co/Ni/Cu–Ln cubanes were pursued; the numerical gain is relative to one prior Co4 catalyst.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: In tubular Ln36M12 water-oxidation clusters, both a variable-valence lanthanide and multivalent cobalt are important: Eu36Co12 is the most active member, while isostructural Ni clusters are much less active or inactive.
review_scope: High-nuclearity Ln36Co12 and Ln36Ni12 clusters (Ln = Eu, Gd, Dy) for electrocatalytic water oxidation.
review_conditions: 0.5 M NaAc/AcOH, pH 5.8, glassy-carbon electrode; Eu36Co12 TON 35, TOF 1.5 s−1, overpotential 0.7 V.
review_caveats: The detailed O–O mechanism is inferred from voltammetry rather than direct intermediate isolation.

title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
review_claim: Lanthanide doping of titanium oxo clusters can improve both stability and photoelectrocatalytic water oxidation relative to undoped clusters, with activity tracking the band gap and being highest for variable-valent Eu.
review_scope: Lanthanide-doped titanium oxo clusters used as molecular models of TiO2 water-oxidation catalysts.
review_conditions: Eu8Ti10: 500 W mercury lamp, 0.2 M NaAc/AcOH, pH 6.0, ITO electrode; reported TON 7581 and TOF 2527 s−1.
review_caveats: Transition-metal doping is separately said to narrow the gap of titanium oxo clusters; the Eu advantage is within this isomorphic Ln series, not a universal ranking of all dopants.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: POM-based all-inorganic open frameworks are assembled either by self-polymerization of POM clusters through shared vertices, edges, or faces, or by joining POM clusters with additional inorganic cations.
review_scope: All-inorganic open frameworks built from polyoxoniobate, polyoxomolybdate, polyoxovanadate, or polyoxotungstate secondary building units.
review_conditions: Aqueous, hydrothermal, or related solution conditions; exact pH, temperature, and cation identity are system-dependent.
review_caveats: Adding extra metal linkers frequently produces dense rather than open packing, so porosity is not guaranteed by the linker strategy alone.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Co-linked {P8W48} crystals can undergo reversible crystal-to-crystal contraction and guest exchange with water, ammonia, and methanol because the ring SBU stays intact while the lattice reorganizes.
review_scope: Co-bridged {P8W48} framework W9 and its dehydrated, rehydrated, ammonia, and methanol phases.
review_conditions: 80 °C under vacuum for dehydration; air for partial rehydration; ammonia vapor about 1 min; methanol vapor 30 min; saturated K2SO4 for two weeks for one rehydrated phase.
review_caveats: Multiple single-crystal routes are documented for this one framework family; the review does not show the same guest set for every {P8W48} phase.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Bridging a Preyssler {P5W30} cluster into an all-inorganic framework preserves reversible multi-electron redox and raises electronic conductivity relative to the discrete cluster, while the bridging metal and encapsulated cation tune the optical response.
review_scope: Preyssler-type {NaP5W30} all-inorganic frameworks bridged by divalent first-row transition metals, especially W12 and the W13 series.
review_conditions: W12 from K14NaP5W30O110 and CoCl2·6H2O at 90 °C in 1 M LiCl at pH 2; W13 by reflux of the potassium salt with metal chlorides at pH 1; photochemical reduction used to keep crystallinity.
review_caveats: Conductivity comparisons are for the reported crystals or pressed pellets. Hydrolytic stability and rigidity are stated for the delocalized-electron frameworks in these studies, not for all POW frameworks.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: In K-linked Preyssler frameworks, occluded PEG can contribute to proton transport through polymer segmental motion, whereas a PAA-containing analogue is the humidity-stable member and reaches higher proton conductivity.
review_scope: Polyoxotungstate frameworks W7a–c based on the Preyssler anion with PEG or polyallylamine guests.
review_conditions: Hydrothermal assembly of the Preyssler salt with KNO3 and the polymer; proton conductivity from impedance spectra and Arrhenius plots.
review_caveats: The segmental-motion explanation is an inference from activation energies. Conductivity and stability differences are specific to these three polymer-containing phases.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Lacunary tungstate precursors can rearrange into larger all-inorganic building units in which metal octahedra fuse by shared edges, not only by single bridging oxygen atoms.
review_scope: Copper–silicotungstate all-inorganic frameworks derived from γ-SiW10, namely W1-Na and W1-K.
review_conditions: Hydrothermal synthesis from the lacunary γ-SiW10 precursor; Na+ or K+ as the framework linker.
review_caveats: The edge-fused connectivity is established for this {Cu4Si2W16} pair. The review does not claim that every lacunary precursor rearranges in the same way.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Morpholinium can template {W72M12X7} all-inorganic frameworks while buffering pH and filling pores, and Co(II) linkers can be postsynthetically oxidized to unstable Co(III) in a reversible single-crystal transformation.
review_scope: Heterometal-linked {W72M12X7} polyoxotungstate frameworks with morpholinium countercations.
review_conditions: One-pot synthesis for Co(II) phases; postsynthetic oxidation for Co(III) phases; morpholinium present as template, buffer, and pore cation.
review_caveats: The Co(III) state is described as unstable, so the oxidized crystals are not presented as a permanently robust redox form.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: An anionic lanthanide–silicotungstate open framework preferentially takes up cationic dyes and, between two cationic dyes, takes up the smaller methylene blue more than rhodamine B.
review_scope: Isostructural frameworks W15-Ln (Ln = La, Pr, Nd), with dye uptake reported for W15-La.
review_conditions: Immersion of crystals for 600 min in mixed aqueous dye solutions of RhB with MB, or MB with MO.
review_caveats: Selectivity is demonstrated for these dye pairs on W15-La. The review does not report isotherms, capacities for other guests, or whether Pr and Nd analogues behave identically.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: POM-based all-inorganic open frameworks are still an early field: structural diversity is narrow and dominated by tungstates, synthesis is mostly conventional solution or hydrothermal/solvothermal chemistry, and many properties remain unexamined.
review_scope: The family of POM-based all-inorganic open frameworks as surveyed through this review.
review_caveats: These are gaps in the reported literature as judged by the authors, not evidence that the missing clusters, methods, or properties are inaccessible.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Open rather than dense POM frameworks are favored by sterically bulky countercations or by intrinsically porous POM secondary building units, whose internal pores propagate into framework channels.
review_scope: POM-based all-inorganic frameworks, especially polyoxotungstates using {P5W30} or {P8W48}.
review_conditions: Porous SBUs are linked by alkali or transition-metal cations; bulky organic cations such as tetramethylammonium can occupy the resulting channels.
review_caveats: Bulky cations enlarge or occupy voids but can also fill channels, so they do not automatically yield guest-accessible porosity.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Formation of suitable POM cluster building units, and therefore of the corresponding all-inorganic frameworks, is generally confined to a narrow pH window and is also sensitive to temperature and cation concentration.
review_scope: Solution and hydrothermal synthesis of POM-based all-inorganic open frameworks, documented in detail for {P8W48}/Ag systems.
review_conditions: For the Ag/{P8W48} series, higher Ag+ with heating to 80 °C versus lower Ag+ without heating, and a further pH change under the latter conditions, select among W11a–W11c.
review_caveats: The review does not give one universal pH interval; the narrow window is a qualitative generalization across reported compounds.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Polyoxoniobate all-inorganic frameworks remain scarce because soluble PONb precursors are lacking and the chemistry is constrained to strongly alkaline conditions.
review_scope: All-inorganic open frameworks based on polyoxoniobate SBUs.
review_conditions: Strongly alkaline reaction media; the {Nb10} series uses Ca2+, Sr2+, or Ba2+ linkers with TMA countercations.
review_caveats: The scarcity is a literature-status statement in this review, not a proof that PONb frameworks are intrinsically impossible outside alkaline conditions.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: In ε-Keggin molybdate microporous frameworks, heating can remove water and ammonia from zigzag micropores without framework collapse, and the resulting guest loss increases O2 uptake while Mo redox responds to H2 or O2.
review_scope: ε-Keggin polyoxomolybdate all-inorganic frameworks Na–Mo–Mn and NH4–Mo–Fe.
review_conditions: Hydrothermal synthesis near 175 °C; N2 sorption after calcination; O2 isotherms under normal pressure; redox heating in H2 or O2.
review_caveats: Surface areas are low, and pore cleaning is described as partial. The redox and sorption behavior is reported for this pair of frameworks, not for all POMo frameworks.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Proton conductivity in hydrophilic-channel POM all-inorganic frameworks increases sharply with relative humidity because water enters the channels and completes hydrogen-bond pathways.
review_scope: Water-mediated proton conduction in open POM frameworks with hydrophilic channels, illustrated by Mo24b, Mo154, and V13a/V13b.
review_conditions: Variable relative humidity; Mo24b studied from about 40–98% RH and 25–95 °C; Mo154 impedance at different RH and temperature; V13a/b at 25 °C and 75–95% RH.
review_caveats: Not all frameworks in the review require mobile water: V7 shows appreciable proton conductivity under anhydrous conditions below the melting point of water. Humidity can also destabilize some PEG-containing Preyssler frameworks.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: In ε-Keggin zeolitic octahedral metal oxides, subatomic changes in linkers and extra-framework cations retune micropore openings and can invert or enhance CO2 versus C2H2 selectivity through size sieving.
review_scope: ε-Keggin POM-based zeolitic octahedral metal oxides (ZOMO), including NH4–ZM, NH4–MM, NH4–NM, and NH4–IM and cation variants.
review_conditions: CO2 and C2H2 isotherms at 273 K; selectivity estimated by IAST.
review_caveats: The selectivity rule is drawn from this ZOMO series. Some members are noted as stable at high temperature and humidity, but adsorption data are not claimed for every composition under all conditions.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: {P8W48} rings function as reusable porous nodes that transition-metal cations stitch into open all-inorganic lattices, with Ag+ concentration, heating, and pH switching between layered and less dense cubic packings.
review_scope: Polyoxotungstate all-inorganic frameworks that use {P8W48} as the main SBU and Mn2+, Co2+, or Ag+ as linkers.
review_conditions: Aqueous Li-buffered or related simple solution conditions; Ag series compared at higher concentration with heating to 80 °C versus lower concentration without heating, plus a pH change.
review_caveats: Channels are often filled by aqua-metal ions, NH4+, Li+/K+, and solvent, so crystallographic cavity size is not the same as permanent porosity.

title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
review_claim: Oxidizing Mn(II) linkers in a {P8W48} framework lowers Cu(II) uptake because the framework charge decreases and bound copper is released.
review_scope: Mn-linked {P8W48} framework W2 and its oxidized form W2ox.
review_conditions: Cation-uptake tests over 24 h, compared for W2 and W2ox.
review_caveats: This charge-uptake relationship is reported for copper on this Mn framework, not as a quantified rule for every redox-active POM framework.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Luminescence dissymmetry is largest when the electric and magnetic transition-dipole strengths are comparable and nearly parallel, so magnetic-dipole-allowed, only partly electric-dipole-allowed 4f–4f bands of chiral Ln(III) complexes typically give much larger glum than purely electric-dipole organic emitters.
review_scope: Chiral luminescent molecules, with emphasis on Ln(III) 4f–4f emission versus organic fluorophores.
review_conditions: Ideal comparison assumes θ = 0 (cosθ = 1) as plotted in Fig. 3; glum = ±2 is complete circular polarization and 0 is unpolarized emission.
review_caveats: Oscillator-strength orders (ED much larger than MD) are general estimates, not measured values for every complex.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: The practical route to usable CPL brightness is to keep a chiral, somewhat low-symmetry Eu(III) site while maximizing absorption and sensitization, as in tetrahedral Eu4 cages and hfa/pybox complexes, rather than maximizing glum alone.
review_scope: Solution Eu(III) polynuclear cages, heteroleptic hfa complexes, and related aggregates aimed at devices or imaging.
review_conditions: Cage spectra at 2.5×10^-6 mol L^-1 in CHCl3; Bn-pybox data in acetonitrile and dichloromethane.
review_caveats: Individual glum and quantum-yield numbers are compound-specific. A later alkyl-ammonium tetrakis(camphorate) reaches glum = −1.54 but is cited for naked-eye detection, not as the brightness optimum.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Solid-state CPL of Ln(III) materials is prone to artifacts from linear polarization, sample anisotropy, excitation geometry, polarizer reflections, and the sample’s own circular dichroism, so an isotropic or carefully corrected measurement is required before a glum value is trusted.
review_scope: Solid films, crystals, pellets, and polymer dispersions of CPL-active Ln(III) compounds.
review_conditions: Distinguish highly ordered samples from randomly oriented powders or polymer films.
review_caveats: Artifact suppression reduces but does not eliminate experimental deviation; multiple spectra are still required. The review does not provide a universal correction protocol beyond pointing to the Stokes–Mueller literature.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Dispersing a preformed chiral Ln complex in a rigid matrix (PMMA, PDMS, or related polymers) is a standard way to move solution CPL into processable solids while often retaining the solution dissymmetry and narrowing thermal or quenching losses.
review_scope: Chiral Ln(III) coordination compounds processed as polymer films or pellets rather than neat powders only.
review_conditions: PMMA thin films and KBr pellets for the Eu/Tb helicates; PDMS for the Yb complexes.
review_caveats: Retention of glum is demonstrated for specific helicates, not guaranteed for every complex. Short-range interactions in the solid can still change CPL relative to solution.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: For Yb(III) NIR CPL, glum of individual crystal-field components changes with temperature mainly because hot bands and Stark components overlap differently, not because the coordination geometry rearranges.
review_scope: Crystal-field-split Yb(III) NIR emitters dispersed in PDMS; the reasoning is expected to apply to other Kramers ions with overlapping Stark CPL.
review_conditions: Variable temperature down to 77 K; no significant structural change assumed.
review_caveats: This temperature mechanism is drawn from one cited Yb/PDMS study. It does not replace humidity or photonic-band-gap effects seen in other solid hosts.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: CPL can be programmed into otherwise achiral Ln complexes or upconversion nanoparticles by embedding them in a chiral host—MOFs, helical gels, cellulose nanocrystals, or doped liquid crystals—whose photonic band gap or host–guest contacts set the handedness and can amplify glum.
review_scope: Achiral molecular Ln complexes and lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles assembled with chiral organic, MOF, or liquid-crystal media.
review_conditions: Upconversion examples use ~974–980 nm excitation. Photonic amplification requires the emission or excitation to overlap a band edge.
review_caveats: Host-induced glum values span orders of magnitude (about 10^-2 for the camphorate MOF guests versus ~0.5 in the optimized liquid crystal) and are not interchangeable. Adding a chiral matrix increases synthetic steps.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Solid-state rigidity can raise quantum yield by suppressing nonradiative decay, but BCPL is not straightforward to report for solids because absorption efficiency is hard to measure, and intermolecular contacts can change glum relative to solution.
review_scope: Processable solid, gel, and composite Ln(III) CPL materials intended for security inks, sensors, and CP-OLEDs.
review_conditions: Comparison of solution versus solid emission on the same complex; absorption efficiency required for solution-style BCPL.
review_caveats: The direction of the quantum-yield change is a general expectation, not quantified for every matrix in the review.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: High glum and high CPL brightness are often opposed: Eu(III) 5D0→7F1 can give glum > 0.1 because it is purely magnetic-dipole, but its low intensity and branching ratio limit brightness, whereas hypersensitive 5D0→7F2 is brighter but usually has a less favorable |μ|/|m| ratio.
review_scope: Eu(III) coordination compounds used as CPL emitters; the same trade-off is stated more generally for Ln(III) complexes.
review_conditions: 5D0→7F1 is the ΔJ = 1 magnetic-dipole transition; 5D0→7F2 is forced electric dipole and hypersensitive.
review_caveats: The explicit algebraic definition of BCPL (Eq. 14) is cited but not reproduced in the Markdown. Promising compounds with glum 0.1–1 and quantum yields above 10% show the trade-off is not absolute.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Efficient antenna sensitization of Eu(III) or Tb(III) requires a ligand triplet roughly 2500–3000 cm^-1 above the accepting Ln excited level so ligand-to-metal energy transfer occurs without strong back-transfer.
review_scope: Mononuclear, polynuclear, polymer, and MOF Ln(III) complexes that rely on organic antenna ligands, illustrated especially for Eu(III) and Tb(III).
review_conditions: Typical path is ligand S0→Sn, IC to S1, ISC to T1, then energy transfer to Ln(III).
review_caveats: The 2500–3000 cm^-1 window is given as an example for Eu(III) or Tb(III), not a universal gap for every Ln ion. Exchange and resonance pathways can operate together.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Ligand-to-Ln energy transfer switches from short-range exchange to longer-range multipolar resonance: exchange needs orbital overlap and is effective below about 4 Å with ΔJ = 0, ±1, whereas dipole–dipole transfer falls as R^-6 and dominates beyond about 4 Å.
review_scope: Nonradiative ligand-to-Ln(III) sensitization in coordination compounds.
review_conditions: Exchange selection rule quoted as ΔJ = 0, ±1 (with J′ ≠ 0 in the review’s wording). Distance threshold about 4 Å.
review_caveats: The review’s sentence that efficiency “decreases as the Ln–ligand distances become short” is inconsistent with the stated <4 Å contribution and is treated as a wording error; the distance rule itself is taken from the accompanying mechanism description and ref. 68.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Eu(III) emission reports site symmetry: 5D0 is nondegenerate, so the number of Stark components of each 5D0→7FJ band reflects the degeneracy of 7FJ, and observation of 5D0→7F0 signals at least one non-centrosymmetric site with one component per such chemical environment.
review_scope: Eu(III) in complexes, glasses, and crystalline hosts used as a spectroscopic probe, including CPL design.
review_conditions: Maximum splitting is 2J+1 for non-Kramers Eu(III); at most three 5D0→7F1 components per non-equivalent site.
review_caveats: Absence of 5D0→7F0 does not by itself prove inversion symmetry if the line is simply too weak to detect.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Chiral Ln(III) complexes are obtained either with enantiopure chiral ligands, which can give optically pure products or diastereomer mixtures, or with polydentate/macrocyclic ligands that form helices whose metal-centered chirality is usually racemic and must be resolved.
review_scope: Solution and solid Ln(III) coordination compounds designed for CPL.
review_conditions: Hard-donor chelates; enantiomer separation is required when the product is racemic.
review_caveats: Chiral ligands do not automatically give a single diastereomer; quasi-racemization of conformations remains a problem unless the geometry is locked.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: For eight- and nine-coordinate Ln(III) complexes with square-antiprism or square-prism geometries, solution CPL is predicted to vanish at twist angles of 0°, 90°, and ±45° and to maximize near ±22.5°, following a sin(4θ) dependence.
review_scope: Chiral macrocyclic Ln(III) complexes of coordination numbers 8 and 9 in solution.
review_conditions: Square antiprism or square prism; θ is the twist angle of the principal axis.
review_caveats: A later Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] example has a torsion near −41.4°, close to the ideal SAP angle, yet very high glum, so twist angle alone does not explain every record value.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: CPL can arise by static coupling when the first coordination sphere itself is chiral, or by dynamic coupling of the Ln ion to ligand-centered transitions even if the coordination polyhedron is achiral; dynamic coupling can produce the larger glum because Ln–ligand covalency is usually small.
review_scope: Ln(III) complexes whose 4f–4f CPL is interpreted by ligand-field coupling, especially camphorate and β-diketonate Eu(III) species.
review_conditions: Static coupling requires a chiral first sphere; dynamic coupling is invoked when an achiral polyhedron still shows CPL or when glum exceeds the twist-angle prediction.
review_caveats: The static-versus-dynamic distinction is a mechanistic interpretation drawn from cited analyses, not a direct measurement in this review. Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] quantum yield remains below about 1%.

title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
review_claim: Multipoint ligand–ligand contacts and extended helical packing can raise both glum and sensitization relative to a mononuclear analogue by locking one chiral conformation and organizing the chromophores.
review_scope: Heteroleptic Eu(III)/Tb(III) β-diketonate complexes with chiral pybox, facam, or bridging phosphine-oxide ligands, in solution or as coordination polymers.
review_conditions: Solution data are solvent- and concentration-specific (for example CD3CN or acetone-d6); the polymer comparison is solid state.
review_caveats: Ligand–ligand locking does not remove the brightness trade-off: some of the highest glum values still have quantum yields below 1%. Tb analogues of the hfa/pybox series stay weakly emissive because of back-transfer.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Controlled 3d-4f cluster growth is pursued by limiting hydrolysis of hydrolysis-prone rare-earth and transition-metal ions with protecting ligands, rather than allowing unrestricted hydroxo/oxo bridging.
review_scope: 3d-4f heterometallic clusters assembled by hydrolysis.
review_conditions: Hydrolytic assembly in the presence of ligands that limit the extent of metal-ion hydrolysis.
review_caveats: The review does not claim that ligand protection fully eliminates uncontrolled hydrolysis.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: The bowl-shaped {Ln19Ni21} unit can dimerize to dumbbell-like Ln42Ni38 or polymerize to helical (Ln18Ni24)n chains when anions, metal ions, or auxiliary ligands bridge the bowls.
review_scope: IDA-protected Ln-Ni clusters based on the {Ln19Ni21} bowl.
review_conditions: Bridging by anions, metal ions, or auxiliary ligands.
review_caveats: Assembly pathways are not established.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: High-throughput synthesis plus machine learning can map a four-parameter space and switch between colossal La-Ni cages by tuning alkali and oxalate, thereby resizing the n × m × l inorganic framework.
review_scope: IDA/oxalate La-Ni cage clusters explored on an automated synthesis workstation.
review_conditions: Four-parameter synthetic space including alkali and oxalate; high-throughput experiments with machine-learning phase diagrams.
review_caveats: The review lists remaining limits: more efficient automation, algorithms for multidimensional data, and richer time-resolved datasets.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Isotropic f7 Gd(III) and relatively weak Gd-3d exchange make IDA-stabilized Gd-Ni and Gd-Co clusters the main magnetocaloric targets in this ligand family, with Gd152Ni14 reported as the largest molecular-cluster −ΔSm.
review_scope: IDA-stabilized Gd-Ni and Gd-Co clusters used as molecular magnetic refrigerants.
review_conditions: −ΔSm values in Table 3 are reported near 2-4.2 K, mostly at 7.0 T and in a few cases at 2.0 T.
review_caveats: The prose and Table 3 disagree on the numerical maximum for the Gd152Ni14 family. Magnetic coupling between centers is still poorly understood.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Encapsulating Gd52Ni56 in a silica shell by a microemulsion route increases the measured magnetocaloric effect and improves processability while keeping the cluster core intact.
review_scope: Microemulsion silica encapsulation of the IDA Gd52Ni56 cluster.
review_conditions: Microemulsion synthesis of monodisperse silica-coated nanoparticles; MCE comparison at low temperature and up to 7 T.
review_caveats: The improvement is reported for this encapsulation example; the review does not generalize a quantitative enhancement factor.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Ni(II), the 3d ion most often used in these IDA 3d-4f clusters, is a poor choice for single-molecule magnets because of its relatively low spin and weak magnetic anisotropy.
review_scope: SMM design within IDA-stabilized 3d-4f clusters that commonly use Ni(II).
review_caveats: This is a design limitation stated by the review, not a survey of measured energy barriers for the tabulated clusters.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Packing many Gd(III) ions into one IDA 3d-Gd cluster, then encapsulating it in a biocompatible polymer, is presented as a route to stronger MRI contrast at lower dose than small-molecule Gd agents.
review_scope: Polymer-encapsulated IDA Gd-Ni clusters as T1 MRI contrast candidates.
review_conditions: Biocompatible polymer encapsulation of Gd52Ni56; in vivo comparison described for PEC-3 versus DTPA-Gd.
review_caveats: The performance claim is tied to the PEC-3 study; the review does not provide a numerical relaxivity in the text.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Partial replacement of Ni by Cd from a CdS support converts Ln52Ni56 into a cocatalyst that separates charge and supplies HER sites, with the Eu analogue giving very high visible-light hydrogen evolution.
review_scope: IDA Ln52Ni56 clusters on CdS for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
review_conditions: Visible-light irradiation at wavelengths of at least 420 nm; Cd substitution from the CdS support.
review_caveats: The rate is for the cited Eu composite, not a general activity of all Ln52Ni56 clusters.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Building-block assembly gives only partial structural control in the IDA system; function-specific heterometallic clusters still require real-time observation of assembly, which soft-ionization high-resolution mass spectrometry can supply.
review_scope: Synthetic control and mechanism studies of IDA 3d-4f clusters.
review_conditions: In-process monitoring, exemplified by soft-ionization high-resolution mass spectrometry.
review_caveats: The mass-spectrometry examples cited for formation dynamics are not all IDA 3d-4f clusters.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Some n × m × l IDA cages contain atomically precise nanoscale channels that have been considered for separation, but that use does not yet exploit the heterometallic function.
review_scope: Porous n × m × l IDA Ln-Ni cages, specifically the separation attempt on Ln96Ni60.
review_caveats: Separation is described as an attempt, not a demonstrated general application, and the prose nuclearity Ln96Ni60 does not match every Table 2 5×5×5 entry.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Under HSAB reasoning, lanthanide ions prefer oxygen donors while borderline Ni(II) binds both nitrogen and oxygen, so multidentate N/O ligands are used to steer mixed-metal hydrolysis.
review_scope: Ligand choice for 3d-4f clusters, especially Ni(II) with lanthanides.
review_caveats: HSAB is used as a design rationale; the same section stresses that coordination outcomes remain poorly predictable.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: In situ transient [M(IDA)] species (M = Ni or Co), not preformed stable complexes, chelate the 3d ion and then use pendant carboxylate oxygens to direct lanthanide hydrolysis and link further [M(IDA)] units.
review_scope: Iminodiacetic acid and derivative ligands with Ni(II) or Co(II) and lanthanides.
review_conditions: [M(IDA)] forms in situ during synthesis rather than being isolated as a stable precursor.
review_caveats: The review treats [M(IDA)] as a transient intermediate inferred from assembly behavior, not as an isolated reagent.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Among discrete high-nuclearity 3d-4f clusters in the authors' CSD screen, iminodiacetic acid and its derivatives account for most structures once the metal count exceeds 50, and nearly all once it exceeds 100.
review_scope: Discrete 3d-4f clusters meeting the stated nuclearity cutoffs in the Cambridge Structural Database screen summarized in Fig. 3.
review_conditions: Screen criterion written as [Ln] > 5 and [TM] > 5, with continuous MOF-type structures excluded.
review_caveats: Percentages reflect this database filter and ligand classification, not a complete census of all 3d-4f compounds.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Under IDA coordination, Ni(II) and Co(II) hydrolyze on a timescale compatible with lanthanides, whereas Zn(II) and Fe(II) tend to precipitate as hydroxides and do not proceed to high-nuclearity 3d-4f clusters.
review_scope: IDA-ligated attempts to make high-nuclearity 3d-4f clusters.
review_conditions: IDA ligand environment compared for Ni(II), Co(II), Zn(II), and Fe(II).
review_caveats: The contrast is qualitative; no hydrolysis pH or concentration window is given for the failing metals.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Anions are used both as charge-balancing structural components and as templates, but multiply charged anions must be kept dilute enough to avoid rapid precipitation with rare-earth ions.
review_scope: IDA-stabilized 3d-4f cluster synthesis using anionic templates.
review_conditions: Controlled concentration of multiply charged anions during assembly.
review_caveats: Too much template anion favors precipitates rather than clusters.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Carbonate commonly binds lanthanides through three oxygen donors to give pentagonal {Ln5} and hexagonal {Ln6} units, while halides can template high-nuclearity cores without directly coordinating the metals.
review_scope: Anion roles in IDA-family 3d-4f clusters.
review_caveats: Not every listed anion produces the same Ln5 or Ln6 motif; those geometries are specifically attributed to carbonate.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Many IDA-stabilized Ln-Ni clusters form tunable n × m × l parallelepiped frameworks whose edges are built by repeating triangular {LnNi3} units.
review_scope: IDA-ligated Ln-Ni parallelepiped cluster families.
review_conditions: Identification of recurring blocks from crystal structures, then assembly; auxiliary anions or ligands differ by entry in Table 2.
review_caveats: Fig. 5 marks some predicted n × m × l topologies as not yet found. Auxiliary ligands change nuclearity even within the same nominal topology.

title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
review_claim: Heart-shaped IDA-family units made from carbonate-centered [Ln5(μ5-CO3)]13+ and cubane-like [Ln3M(μ3-OH)4] assemble into a Gd44Co28 crown and a larger Gd95Co60 cage.
review_scope: Carbonate- and hydroxide-bridged Gd-Co clusters stabilized in the IDA system.
review_conditions: Level-by-level assembly of the heart-shaped motif as proposed in Fig. 6.
review_caveats: A further series from the same group is stated to be unpublished and in preparation, so only the reported crown and cage should be treated as established examples.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Varying ligand substituents changes electronic effects and steric hindrance around rare-earth ions, which tunes coordination symmetry and polarizability and thereby macroscopic optical or magnetic properties.
review_scope: Rare-earth coordination complexes whose properties are set by the first coordination sphere, including Er(III) organometallic SMMs and luminescent complexes accessed by ligand exchange.
review_conditions: Substituent steric series on COT for Er(III); stepwise exchange between rigid and flexible ligands.
review_caveats: Each outcome is illustrated by a 2025 case rather than a quantified general scaling law.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Parity-allowed d–f emission of Ce3+ and Eu2+ is broad and strongly crystal-field dependent, and phenyl or benzophenone units can switch the pathway from 5d–4f emission toward 2MLCT, delayed d–f emission, mixed ligand fluorescence/phosphorescence, or double-delayed doublet emission.
review_scope: Ce3+ and Eu2+ molecular emitters, including S-coordinating poly(mercaptoimidazolyl)borate Ce(III) complexes.
review_conditions: Ligands that introduce phenyl or benzophenone energy levels.
review_caveats: Not every Ce3+/Eu2+ complex undergoes the MLCT switch; the new emission mode is a first report in the cited work.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Strong axial crystal fields from bulky, electron-rich ligands, together with removal or rigidification of equatorial donors, suppress zero-field quantum tunneling and lengthen magnetic relaxation in Dy(III) single-molecule magnets.
review_scope: Dy(III) mononuclear and binuclear SMMs with axial oxygen donors and controlled equatorial ligands.
review_conditions: Absence of laterally coordinated chloride in the bis(amide) case; hydrogen-bond and π–π stabilization of a linear μ-Cl bridge with axial alkoxides in the aminopyridine dimer.
review_caveats: Barrier heights and hysteresis temperatures are not restated numerically in the review.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Strong magnetic anisotropy is not restricted to macrocyclic ligands: enlarging and rigidifying the side chains of the flexible open-chain ligand PyMTA can tune lanthanide magnetic anisotropy.
review_scope: Lanthanide complexes of open-chain PyMTA-type ligands and hollow 3d–4f clusters for magnetism or magnetic refrigeration.
review_conditions: Larger, more rigid coordinating side chains on PyMTA; hollow cluster architectures from NO3− and carbonate subunits.
review_caveats: The macrocycle exception and the magnetocaloric hollow-cluster result are distinct examples and should not be merged into one structure–function rule.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Coupling DFT or multireference calculations, and machine-learning loops, with experiment is presented as a shift from empirical rare-earth design to theory-guided prediction of reactivity, magnetic coupling, electrochemistry, and high oxidation states.
review_scope: Computational and data-driven design of rare-earth molecules, clusters, and doped MOF electrodes.
review_conditions: DFT; CASSCF/NEVPT2 for the ionisation quotient; iterative experiment–learning over 780 condition sets for the nested cluster.
review_caveats: The outlook later notes that theoretical predictions still disagree with experiment, so these criteria are not treated as fully mature.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: External stimuli switch rare-earth molecular materials by coordination-bond rearrangement, supramolecular reorganization, electronic rearrangement, or structural relaxation, and orthogonal stimuli can address different channels in one assembly.
review_scope: Stimuli-responsive lanthanide nanoparticles and Eu-MOF heterostructures for dynamic luminescence.
