review_conditions: Changes in pH, temperature, or illumination for Eu-NPs; sequential solvent then LED stimulation for the SSR Eu-MOF.
review_caveats: Orthogonality is demonstrated for the cited Eu-NP system, not asserted for every multistimulus lanthanide material.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Photoirradiation that generates ligand or framework radicals can couple optical switching to static and dynamic magnetism in Yb(III) and Dy(III) molecule-based magnets.
review_scope: Photoactive lanthanide coordination polymers, 2D Dy-SMM MOFs, and viologen-containing lanthanide cages.
review_conditions: UV or other photoirradiation sufficient to generate radicals or charge-transfer states.
review_caveats: Magnetic-barrier gains are not quantified in the review, and the cage example is catalytic rather than an SMM.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Temperature can retune ligand triplet energy through restricted molecular-rotor motion, so one AIE ligand selectively sensitizes Tb(III) or Eu(III) and produces multicolor switching.
review_scope: Mixed Tb/Eu MOFs with rotor-containing AIE ligands, and radioluminescent ratiometric thermometers.
review_conditions: Temperature control of intramolecular rotor motion or of energy-transfer efficiency.
review_caveats: The selective sensitization pathway is reported for the cited rotor MOF, not as a universal thermometer design rule.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: An external magnetic field can modulate rare-earth luminescence and circular polarization when the complex has strong anisotropy or a chiral lattice, contrary to the assumption that 4f emission is magnetically insensitive.
review_scope: Chiral Eu(III) hybrids and magnetically anisotropic Dy(III) complexes.
review_conditions: Applied magnetic field; chiral organic cation for the Eu MPL example; bidentate coordination that enforces Dy anisotropy.
review_caveats: The Eu MPL observation is a first room-temperature report in this review and lacks a reference number in the Markdown. Field strengths are not given.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Hydrostatic pressure can raise Eu(III) quantum yield by shortening the ligand–metal distance, strengthening hydrogen bonds and π–π contacts, suppressing nonradiative decay, and improving energy transfer.
review_scope: Compressible europium carboxylate MOFs, specifically Eu(BTC) hydrate.
review_conditions: High pressure, with the stated performance at 9.2 GPa.
review_caveats: The numerical PLQY is for this framework under pressure; ambient reversibility and generality to other Eu-MOFs are not established in the review.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Combining rigid aryl rings with flexible alkyl chains lowers the melting point of single-molecule magnets while preserving crystallinity, enabling a reversible crystal–liquid–glass–glass-ceramic–crystal cycle and melt blending of luminescence with magnetism.
review_scope: Molecular SMMs whose ligands contain both rigid benzene units and flexible alkyl chains.
review_conditions: Mild heating through the stated phase-transition cycle; melt mixing of rare-earth complexes.
review_caveats: Retention of SMM function through every phase is asserted for the cited system; processing windows are not tabulated.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Soft S, Se, and Te donors form luminescent Ce(III) complexes outside the usual O/N ligand set; sulfur coordination stabilizes Ce 5d orbitals and red-shifts emission, while bulky N-alkyl groups increase ligand-field splitting toward deep-red emission beyond 700 nm.
review_scope: Luminescent Ce(III) complexes with soft chalcogen donors, especially S-coordinated systems whose N-alkyl bulk is varied.
review_conditions: Soft S/Se/Te coordination; alkyl substitution on ligand nitrogen atoms.
review_caveats: The deep-red >700 nm result is tied to the sterically enforced mononuclear structure in the cited S-donor example, not to every soft-donor Ce complex.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Ligands with two environmentally switchable excited states, or with separate π/hydrogen-bond and metal-emission channels, can couple sensing with a second function such as proton conduction, gas separation, or electrocatalysis in one rare-earth framework.
review_scope: Multifunctional Eu-, Tb-, and Ce-based MOFs and flexible MOF–carbon electrodes.
review_conditions: Humidity for ESIPT switching; CNT–Ce-MOF electronic coupling in a PVA electrode; microporous hybrid-ligand pores for C2H2/CO2.
review_caveats: The review later warns that optical, electronic, and magnetic functions in integrated systems can compete, so dual function does not imply synergistic optimization.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Solution-processable rare-earth molecular emitters can reach near-unity exciton use in blue devices, and donor–acceptor surface ligands can supply the charge transport that insulating rare-earth nanocrystals otherwise lack.
review_scope: Rare-earth molecular and nanocrystal optoelectronic emitters.
review_conditions: Octahedral pyrazolylborate Eu complex for the exciton-utilization claim; carbazole and diphenylphosphine surface functionalization for charge injection.
review_caveats: Device metrics other than the approximate exciton utilization are not extracted in the review text.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: The review identifies four field-level bottlenecks: insufficient in-situ observation of dynamic structural change, immature theory that still misses experiment, unclear and often competitive multifunctional coupling, and a performance–stability trade-off that confines many systems to inert atmospheres.
review_scope: Rare-earth molecule-based functional materials as summarized for 2025, especially dynamic and multifunctional systems intended for devices.
review_caveats: These are the authors’ field assessment, not measurements from a single comparative study.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: π-bound heavy p-block ligands (Sb, Bi, Ge, Sn) in f-element sandwich complexes add spatial and electronic ligand-field control beyond lighter congeners, strengthen spin–orbit coupling, and increase magnetic anisotropy.
review_scope: f-element sandwich complexes using π-coordination of Sb, Bi, Ge, or Sn.
review_conditions: π-coordination mode rather than classical O/N donors.
review_caveats: The anisotropy gain is stated as a design trend across refs. 35–37; numerical barriers are not given in the review.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Installing assembly-active, responsive, or catalytic sites on ligands couples the coordination sphere to higher-order function, including solid-state CPL, size-selective rare-earth separation, and exposed 3d–4f catalytic sites.
review_scope: Functional-ligand design of rare-earth complexes, macrocycles, and 3d–4f coordination clusters.
review_conditions: Alkyl–alkyl assembly for CPL; macrocyclic carboxylates for size selection; visible light and displaceable coordinated solvent for the Co–Gd CO2 reduction example.
review_caveats: These are parallel design examples, not one ligand motif that simultaneously delivers CPL, separation, and catalysis.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Anionic templates and recognition interfaces can steer hierarchical or confined assembly of rare-earth clusters and track coordination in real time through luminescence.
review_scope: Template- and microenvironment-directed assembly of heterometallic rare-earth clusters and carboxylate frameworks.
review_conditions: Anion templates; channel-wall pyridine/hydroxyl arrays; hydrogen-bonding anion transporters with BDC.
review_caveats: Cluster topology and iodine uptake are case-specific; the review does not give a general template-to-topology map.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Interfacial coordination and noncovalent ‘ionic glue’ assembly graft rare-earth complexes onto surfaces, MOFs, helices, or nanoparticles and transfer chirality or electronic structure across the interface.
review_scope: Surface, MOF-on-MOF, helical-nanoribbon, and nanoparticle assemblies of rare-earth complexes.
review_conditions: Au(111) electrostatic deposition; imine-mediated MOF-on-MOF grafting; interfacial coordination on helical nanoribbons; opposite-charge nanoparticle assembly.
review_caveats: Each interface uses a different driving force; the review does not claim one universal grafting protocol.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Spontaneous symmetry breaking through π–π and C–H···π contacts can resolve an achiral europium complex into homochiral aggregates more effectively than conventional chiral resolution.
review_scope: Achiral lanthanide complexes and cages that crystallize or assemble through directional noncovalent contacts or chiral additives.
review_conditions: Spontaneous assembly of EuNTA; amino-acid chiral induction for octahedral cages.
review_caveats: The superiority claim is qualitative and demonstrated on EuNTA rather than shown to be general for all achiral lanthanide complexes.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Lanthanide contraction, combined with a rigid peptide pocket and hydrophobic self-assembly, can amplify small ionic-radius differences into selective aggregation and rare-earth separation.
review_scope: Peptide-based lanthanide recognition and separation, specifically the LBTLLA system.
review_conditions: Rigid peptide pocket, hydrophobic and electrostatic assembly into micrometer-scale aggregates.
review_caveats: Presented as a designed example based on lanthanide contraction, not a universal separation process for every ligand class.

title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
review_claim: Ligand substituents and assembly can redirect antenna energy flow: an intermediate charge-transfer state can sustain efficient Eu3+ sensitization even when the S1–T1 gap is outside the usual optimum, while aggregation or mechanical confinement shortens the donor–acceptor path.
review_scope: Antenna-sensitized lanthanide luminescence, especially Eu3+ complexes, cages, and mechanically interlocked emitters.
review_conditions: Substituent control of CT states; aggregation of AIE ligands; short antenna–metal distances enforced by a mechanical bond.
review_caveats: The review does not specify numerical energy gaps or transfer rates for these 2025 cases.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Ligand-controlled hydrolysis of lanthanide ions, using high pH and multidentate supporting ligands, assembles hydroxide clusters around a cubane-like [Ln4(μ3-OH)4]8+ motif, and higher-nuclearity products that can be built from those motifs commonly contain small anions that the authors interpret as templates.
review_scope: Lanthanide hydroxide clusters, lanthanide-exclusive or later extended to 3d–4f species.
review_conditions: High-pH hydrolysis with multidentate ligands; small anions present in nearly all higher-nuclearity clusters that are formally assembled from smaller motifs.
review_caveats: The Account treats templating as a structural inference from the frequent presence of anions, not as a fully proven mechanism for every cluster.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Encapsulating one nanosized heterometallic cluster in a silica nanoshell gives monodisperse core–shell particles that stabilize the molecule, reduce magnetic interactions between clusters, and slightly increase −ΔSM relative to the unprotected parent.
review_scope: Processable silica-passivated nanoparticles of individual high-nuclearity 3d–4f molecular clusters, illustrated for Ni–Gd and Fe–Gd clusters.
review_conditions: Microemulsion encapsulation; one cluster core per silica nanoshell; MCE compared with the unprotected crystalline or bulk cluster.
review_caveats: Described as a preliminary, system-specific attempt. The enhancement is small, and increased Fe(III) zero-field splitting is an additional effect that is not claimed to be generally beneficial for MCE.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Lanthanide hydroxide cluster assembly is too sensitive to ligand identity, ligand/metal ratio, anion templates, pH, temperature, and reaction time for reliable prediction, and clusters with nuclearity above 25 remain few despite recognized modular cubane-based motifs.
review_scope: Rational synthesis of giant lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters for magnetic cooling.
review_caveats: The C60-like supercluster is a design proposal only. Magnetic-cooler performance still also requires high spin density, low anisotropy, and weak coupling, which are not guaranteed by nuclearity alone.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Hydrothermal or solvothermal conditions let simple carboxylates, which precipitate with lanthanides under ambient pressure before hydrolysis, dissolve enough to support slow ligand-controlled hydrolysis and growth of giant clusters.
review_scope: Lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters supported by simple carboxylates such as acetate, propionate, nicotinate, chloroacetate, and benzoate.
review_conditions: Hydro/solvothermal synthesis; hydrolysis-limiting carboxylate ligands whose lanthanide salts are poorly soluble at ambient pressure.
review_caveats: Assembly remains sensitive to ligand/metal ratio, pH, temperature, and time; nuclearity above 25 is still uncommon.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Polyalcohols and related O-donor ligands, previously little used for this purpose, can support high-nuclearity lanthanide and 4f–3d hydroxide clusters under hydro/solvothermal conditions, and the ligand present in the product may be generated in situ from a polyalcohol precursor.
review_scope: Hydroxide clusters of lanthanides, including heterometallic Mn, Fe, and related ions, supported by polyalcohols or amine-bisalcohol derivatives.
review_conditions: Hydro/solvothermal heating; ligands may be used as supplied or transformed during the reaction.
review_caveats: Most outcomes are individual isolations; ligand transformation (for example GlcNAc to Chromogen I) is case-specific and not a general requirement.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Preformed transition-metal complexes of chelating ligands can act as metalloligands to control subsequent lanthanide hydrolysis and give high-nuclearity 3d–4f clusters, whereas earlier Schiff-base metalloligands usually stopped at low nuclearity; the same ligand system can still change composition with pressure and pH.
review_scope: Heterometallic 3d–4f hydroxide clusters assembled with stable chelate metalloligands, especially Ni–IDA, rather than Schiff-base metalloligands.
review_conditions: Chelating ligand first forms a stable transition-metal complex; hydrolysis then proceeds under hydrothermal or, in the compared case, ambient-pressure conditions.
review_caveats: Schiff-base versus IDA is a literature contrast cited by the authors, not a head-to-head experiment in one reaction series. Product identity also depends on lanthanide ion and pH.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Small oxoanion templates are essential for high-nuclearity lanthanide-containing clusters, but their concentration must stay low; slow release by in situ ligand decomposition or uptake of atmospheric CO2 avoids precipitating lanthanide salts and allows modular growth.
review_scope: Giant lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters templated by nitrate, carbonate, and related small anions.
review_conditions: Low template concentration; hydro/solvothermal in situ anion generation or atmospheric CO2 absorption rather than stoichiometric addition of the anion salt.
review_caveats: The same ligand system is highly condition-sensitive: La versus smaller Pr, or a higher pH, switches among La20Ni30, Pr20Ni21, and Gd54Ni54. Template origin is often inferred, not always independently quantified.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Several templating anions, including mixed anion sets, locally organize recognizable smaller hydroxide units and sit in cages or cavities of the finished cluster, so the anion combination changes the assembled architecture.
review_scope: High-nuclearity lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters whose cores are formally assemblies of cubanes, square pyramids, or related small hydroxide units.
review_conditions: Mixed or multiple small anions (Cl−/NO3−, ClO4−/CO32−, or several ClO4−) present during assembly and located crystallographically inside the core.
review_caveats: Functions (charge balance, geometry, fragment templating) are assigned from crystal structures. Markdown formulas for several of these clusters are corrupted, so exact stoichiometries should be checked against the cited papers.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: For high-nuclearity Gd(III)-exclusive clusters, gravimetric magnetocaloric effect, reported as −ΔSM, generally increases with unpaired-electron density, so small, light ligands and a high metal/ligand mass ratio are preferred over heavier ligands or large anions.
review_scope: Molecular coolants based on high-nuclearity, weakly anisotropic Gd(III)-exclusive hydroxide clusters, evaluated by isothermal magnetic entropy change.
review_conditions: Comparison at ΔH = 70 kOe; spin density expressed as unpaired electrons per gram.
review_caveats: The linear density trend is qualified in the same section by magnetic coupling. The Markdown assigns 41.8 and 43.6 J kg−1 K−1 inconsistently among Gd27, Gd48, and related clusters, so those secondary numbers should not be used without the original papers.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: Within Gd(III) clusters of comparable design, stronger intracluster antiferromagnetic coupling lowers −ΔSM relative to the value expected from spin density, whereas very weak coupling lets −ΔSM approach the calculated full spin entropy.
review_scope: High-nuclearity Gd(III) hydroxide clusters whose MCE is compared with spin density and bulk susceptibility (Weiss θ).
review_conditions: Isothermal entropy change compared with nR ln(2S+1)-type theoretical limits and with the sign and magnitude of antiferromagnetic coupling.
review_caveats: Weiss temperatures are bulk indicators, not a full exchange Hamiltonian. One later sentence in the Markdown also quotes −ΔSM = 41.8 J kg−1 K−1 and θ = −3.57 for Gd48, which conflicts with an earlier numerical assignment and should be verified.

title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
review_claim: In 3d–Gd(III) clusters, Gd(III) weakens the usually strong 3d–3d exchange, and a higher unpaired-electron density still tracks a larger gravimetric −ΔSM, but antiferromagnetic coupling and transition-metal crystal-field effects can cut the observed entropy well below the spin-only limit.
review_scope: High-nuclearity 3d–Gd(III) hydroxide clusters intended as cryogenic molecular coolers.
review_conditions: Gravimetric −ΔSM at ΔH = 70 kOe; comparisons among acetate-supported Ni/Co/Zn/Cu–Gd clusters and larger Ni–Gd clusters.
review_caveats: The Co versus Ni spin argument is a suggested interpretation for one pair. Crystal-field and antiferromagnetic contributions are not separated experimentally for every compound. Some formulas and reference numbers in this section are garbled.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Tb(III) and Dy(III) are the preferred lanthanide centers for high-performance rare-earth SMMs because strong 4f spin-orbit coupling makes the crystal field a perturbation and yields large single-ion anisotropy compared with early 3d cluster SMMs.
review_scope: Mononuclear and polynuclear Ln-SMMs, especially phthalocyanine complexes of Tb and Dy.
review_conditions: Performance is discussed through Ueff and TB; TB is defined as the highest temperature at which magnetization hysteresis can be observed, subject to field sweep rate.
review_caveats: The review does not claim every Tb or Dy complex is an SMM; ligand-field geometry must still be optimized.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Approximate D4d coordination in [LnW10O36]9- does not reproduce the SMM behavior of [LnPc2]-.
review_scope: Lindqvist-type and related Keggin-derived Ln polyoxometalates versus double-decker Ln phthalocyanines.
review_caveats: The review does not specify which relaxation parameters differ, only that the SMM behavior is completely different.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Pentagonal-bipyramidal Dy SMMs with approximate D5h symmetry provide strong axial crystal fields and are associated with some of the higher reported barriers and blocking temperatures in this review.
review_scope: Mononuclear Dy(III) SMMs in pentagonal-bipyramidal (D5h) coordination.
review_conditions: Axial anionic donors with a five-donor equatorial plane are the structural pattern highlighted.
review_caveats: Individual Ueff and TB values are molecule-specific; the review does not give one universal barrier for all D5h complexes. The text uses 'pentagonal biconical' for this geometry.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Ln phthalocyanines are commonly made by halogen synthesis, metallation of free-base ligands, mono-Pc routes, or axial substitution, including high-temperature template condensation of phthalonitrile with rare-earth acetates and vacuum conversion of single-deckers to triple-deckers.
review_scope: Synthesis of single-, double-, and triple-decker rare-earth phthalocyanines.
review_conditions: Template condensation at 280-290 °C; lutetium single-decker thermolysis at 400 °C and 1 Torr; alternative sublimation at 300-420 °C and about 10^-6 Torr for Ln = La, Nd, Eu, Gd, Dy, Er, Yb, Lu.
review_caveats: The review names the halogen method but does not reproduce its procedure. Yields and selectivity are not quantified.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Vacuum evaporation, spin coating, and Langmuir-Blodgett deposition are the established routes for studying thin films of metal phthalocyanines, alongside solvothermal synthesis of LnPc.
review_scope: Thin-film and solvothermal processing of metal and lanthanide phthalocyanines.
review_caveats: No film-thickness, substrate, or magnetic-performance comparison among the three deposition methods is provided.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Ln(III) 4f charge density in the Ising-limit ground state is ellipsoidal rather than spherical, and for oblate ions such as Tb(III) and Dy(III) axial ligand electron density is particularly effective at generating large magnetic anisotropy.
review_scope: Design of ligand fields for trivalent lanthanide SMMs, especially Tb and Dy phthalocyanines and other axial complexes.
review_conditions: The model refers to the Ising-limit ground-state charge density and an effective point-charge electrostatic picture.
review_caveats: The review states the axial-ligand preference explicitly for oblate Tb/Dy; it does not spell out the complementary equatorial-ligand rule for prolate ions in the readable text. Gd3+ is isotropic and is not grouped with the oblate ions.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Ln-SMM magnetism is highly sensitive to small coordination changes and is regulated mainly through uniaxial anisotropy and intermolecular interactions, experimentally by choice of Tb/Dy and by the ligand or external field.
review_scope: Tb- and Dy-based SMMs.
review_caveats: No quantitative tolerance for bond-length or angle changes is given.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: Zero-field quantum tunneling in TbPc2 produces butterfly hysteresis with very small low-temperature remanence and coercivity, limiting its use in high-density memory.
review_scope: TbPc2 and closely related double-decker Tb phthalocyanine SMMs.
review_conditions: Low temperature and near-zero magnetic field.
review_caveats: The statement is specific to TbPc2 behavior as reviewed; it is not a claim that all Tb SMMs lack remanence.

title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
review_claim: A dysprosocenium cation [(Cp^iPr5)Dy(Cp*)]+ raised the hysteresis temperature to 80 K, above the 77 K boiling point of liquid nitrogen, with Ueff of 1541 cm^-1, the highest-performing SMM highlighted in this review.
review_scope: The organometallic Dy single-ion magnet [(Cp^iPr5)Dy(Cp*)][B(C6F5)4] as the record case in this review.
review_conditions: Hysteresis comparison is at 77 K as shown for this salt; Cp^iPr5 is penta-isopropylcyclopentadienyl and Cp* is pentamethylcyclopentadienyl.

ligand_basis: reagent role contains ligand; empty is not evidence of absence
time: 30 min ligand deprotonation, then 1 h after metal addition
vessel_or_method: solution synthesis in methanol/water
synthesis_procedure: NaOH (0.1 g, 2.50 mmol) was dissolved in methanol (10 mL) and added in a single portion to a methanol solution (10 mL) of 2-acetylcyclopentanone (Haccp, 3; 0.27 mL, 2.27 mmol). The mixture was stirred for 30 min at ambient temperature. [Y(NO3)3·6H2O] (1; 0.28 g, 0.75 mmol) dissolved in methanol (10 mL) and water (5 mL) was added dropwise, and stirring was continued for 1 h. The solution volume was reduced by half, water (25 mL) was added, and the precipitate was filtered off, washed with water (30 mL), and dried in vacuum. Colorless crystals of 4 suitable for X-ray diffraction were obtained by slow evaporation of a diethyl ether solution at ambient temperature.
workup_and_crystallization: volume reduced by half; water (25 mL) added; precipitate filtered, washed with water (30 mL), dried in vacuum; single crystals from slow evaporation of diethyl ether at ambient temperature

title: Synthesis of two lanthanide clusters LnIII4 (Gd4 and Dy4) with [2 × 2] square grid shape: Magnetocaloric effect and slow magnetic relaxation behaviors

vessel_or_method: stirring then slow evaporation in a desiccator
synthesis_procedure: A mixture of Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.1 mmol) and H2L (0.1 mmol) in 20 mL methanol/dichloromethane (1:1 v/v) was stirred at room temperature for 4 h. title: New wheel-shaped Ln6 clusters for conversion of CO2 and magnetic properties
ligand_basis: reagent role contains ligand; empty is not evidence of absence
temperature: 343 K (solvothermal), then cooled to room temperature
time: ultrasonication 30 min, then 24 h at 343 K
vessel_or_method: 0.02 L sealed glass vial; ultrasound then solvothermal heating
synthesis_procedure: Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (5×10−5 mol) was added to a solution of triethanolamine (5×10−5 mol) in 0.01 L acetonitrile, then triethylamine (3×10−5 L) was added. The mixture was sealed in a 0.02 L glass vial, ultrasonicated for 30 min, heated at 343 K for 24 h, and slowly cooled to room temperature to give yellow block-shaped crystals.
workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature afforded yellow block-shaped crystals suitable for X-ray crystallography.
property_summary: dc susceptibility shows χMT = 47.40 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K, remaining nearly constant to 20 K then falling to 18.24 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd coupling. Magnetization reaches 42.17 Nβ at 2.0 K and 8 T. A relatively large magnetocaloric effect is observed (−ΔSm max = 41.43 J kg−1 K−1 at 3.0 K and 7.0 T). UV–vis absorption of 1 in ethanol is blue-shifted versus free H3L, with a peak near 209 nm assigned to a π→σ* transition.

synthesis_procedure: To a suspension of H4daps (0.200 g, 0.464 mmol) in methanol (25 mL), (CH3)4N(OH)·5H2O (0.173 g, 0.928 mmol) was added. The yellow solution was stirred for 10 min, then TbCl3·6H2O (0.173 g, 0.464 mmol) was added. The mixture was stirred for 4 h at room temperature, precipitating a small portion of solid Tb2Cl (0.019 g), which was filtered and air-dried. Magnetization at 2 K does not saturate at 5 T. No in-phase or out-of-phase ac peaks at 1400 Hz under 0 or 1000 Oe, so the neat sample is not an SMM.

title: Influence of Energy Barriers in Triangular Dysprosium Single-Molecule Magnets through Different Substitutions on a Nitrophenolate-Type Coligand

The resulting orange solution gave well-formed dark red crystals by vapor diffusion of diethyl ether into the mother liquor over one week at ambient temperature. The crystals are a 50:50 disordered pair of [Dy3(Hhmb)4(μ3-OMe)2(OMe)(2-NP)]+ and [Dy3(Hhmb)4(μ3-OMe)2(2-NP)]+ with three chloride counterions.

property_summary: Trinuclear Dy(III) SMM. Room-temperature χMT is close to the value for three uncoupled Dy(III) ions and decreases on cooling, consistent with weak antiferromagnetic interactions and/or anisotropy. Under zero dc field, complex 1 shows frequency-dependent out-of-phase susceptibility with an effective barrier of 12.18 K. A small applied dc field has little effect, so zero-field QTM is not efficient. The low barrier is attributed to noncoplanar anisotropy axes rather than a toroidal SMT arrangement.

vessel_or_method: Schlenk/argon; ethanol extraction of blue species; CH2Cl2 sonication; hexane layering
synthesis_procedure: HMq (318 mg, 2 mmol), CrCl3·6H2O (266 mg, 1 mmol), and 4-hydroxybenzonitrile (238 mg, 2 mmol) were refluxed in absolute ethanol (30 mL) for 6 h. After neutralization with triethylamine and addition of water (100 mL), the precipitate was redissolved in ethanol; filtration and rotary evaporation gave a blue product. Then 50 mg of the blue product was reacted with 150 mg of Eu(hfac)2(CH3COO)(H2O)2 in 30 mL CH2Cl2 with sonication for 15 min. After filtration, concentrated CH2Cl2 solutions were layered with n-hexane to afford blue crystals. Complex 6 was not characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction.
workup_and_crystallization: Aqueous precipitation, ethanol redissolution of blue fraction, rotary evaporation; n-hexane layering onto CH2Cl2 to blue crystals.
property_summary: Cr-sensitized Eu(III) linelike emission (principal band 613 nm; additional bands 535, 591, 651, 699 nm). Φem = 0.6% in degassed CH2Cl2. 3 equiv F− increases solution lifetime from 584 to 612 μs.

title: The synthesis of a 3d–4f polynuclear metal cluster under microwave irradiation: crystal structure and magnetic property of [La3Ni6(IDA)6(OH)6(H2O)12]·3NO3·15H2O (IDA = iminodiacetate)
reagent_names: ["nickel(II) nitrate hexahydrate","iminodiacetic acid","lanthanum(III) nitrate hexahydrate","sodium hydroxide"]
ligand_basis: reagent role contains ligand; empty is not evidence of absence
temperature: 100 °C (microwave or reflux); crystallization at room temperature
time: microwave 30 min, then 1 day crystallization; reflux 3 days, then 2 weeks crystallization
vessel_or_method: 35 mL quartz vessel, microwave irradiation (5–10 psi); alternative 25 mL conical flask reflux
synthesis_procedure: Microwave route (primary): Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.581 g, 2.0 mmol) and iminodiacetic acid (0.266 g, 2.0 mmol) were dissolved in 8 mL deionized water and stirred for 10 min. La(NO3)3·6H2O (0.866 g, 2.0 mmol) and 8 mL chromatogram-pure acetonitrile were added. The pH was slowly adjusted to about 7.0–7.5 with 1.0 mol L−1 NaOH. The mixture was sealed in a 35 mL quartz vessel and heated at 100 °C under microwave irradiation for 30 min (pressure about 5–10 psi). The resulting pellucid solution was evaporated at room temperature for one day to give light-green flake-shaped crystals in 40.0% yield based on La(NO3)3. Alternative reflux route: the same reagent mixture was transferred to a 25 mL conical flask, refluxed at 100 °C for 3 days, cooled at 1.0 °C min−1, and the filtrate evaporated at room temperature; crystals formed after two weeks in 28.5% yield based on La(NO3)3.
workup_and_crystallization: Microwave product: pellucid solution evaporated at room temperature for one day, light-green flake crystals. Reflux product: cooled at 1.0 °C min−1; filtrate evaporated at room temperature for two weeks.
yield: 40.0% (microwave, based on La(NO3)3); 28.5% (reflux, based on La(NO3)3)
property_summary: Cage-shaped ferromagnetic La3Ni6 cluster. Magnetism arises from six Ni(II) ions (La(III) is diamagnetic). χmT is nearly constant from 75–300 K, then rises at low T due to ferromagnetic Ni···Ni exchange via syn–anti carboxylato bridges in a hexagonal Ni6 ring; a slight drop below 2.8 K is attributed to intercluster antiferromagnetism, ZFS, and/or saturation. MAGPACK fit of Hamiltonian (1) gives J = +0.50 cm−1, D = 0.90 cm−1, g = 2.18.

synthesis_procedure: Main text: hydrothermal reaction of Dy(NO3)3·6H2O, Cr(NO3)3·9H2O, Na2SO4 and piperazine in a 2:1:3:4 molar ratio; experimental details are given in the ESI. SI: all analytical-grade reagents were used as received. A mixture of Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.228 g, 0.50 mmol), Cr(NO3)3·9H2O (0.100 g, 0.25 mmol), Na2SO4 (0.106 g, 0.75 mmol), piperazine (0.086 g, 1.0 mmol) and water (10 mL) was stirred at room temperature for 30 min, transferred to a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel vessel, and heated at 170 °C for 3 days under autogenous pressure. After slow cooling to room temperature, cube-shaped red crystals of 1 were obtained. Yield 0.136 g (62% based on Dy(NO3)3). Elemental analysis found C 2.86, H 2.23, N 1.45%; C4H40N2O42S6Cr2Dy4 requires C 2.77, H 2.32, N 1.61%. IR (KBr) νmax/cm−1: 3384, 1654, 1608, 1436, 1234, 1091, 1051, 987, 644, 597 and 554.
workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature afforded cube-shaped red crystals.
property_summary: Compound 1 is a sulfate-based single-molecule magnet. DC susceptibility indicates dominant antiferromagnetic interactions arranged ferrimagnetically, with thermal depopulation of Dy(III) Stark levels and a large uncompensated spin ground state. Magnetization does not saturate and M vs H/T curves do not superimpose, consistent with anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states. Zero-field ac susceptibility is strongly frequency dependent (φ = 0.19), and the relaxation follows an Arrhenius law. A large Cole–Cole α at 3.0 K indicates a broad distribution and likely multiple relaxation processes associated with two crystallographically distinct Dy(III) sites.

synthesis_procedure: General procedure for 1–4: D-PhGlyH (322 mg, 2.12 mmol, 0.8 eq.) was dissolved in a stirred solution of KOtBu (893 mg, 7.96 mmol, 3 eq.) in 20 mL methanol. Ph2acacH (714 mg, 3.18 mmol, 1.2 eq.) was added, turning the colourless solution yellow. After 15 min stirring, [DyCl3·(H2O)6] (1.00 g, 2.65 mmol, 1 eq.) in 20 mL methanol was added dropwise, forming a flaky white precipitate. The mixture was stirred overnight at room temperature; the precipitate was filtered off, washed with methanol (3 × 5 mL) and air-dried. The yellow solid of 1 was extracted with 5 mL dichloromethane, filtered, cooled to −80 °C and layered with 20 mL n-hexane, giving yellow single crystals after 1–4 days.

property_summary: Dc χT ≈ 70.0 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (expected 70.85 for five uncoupled Dy(III)); χT decreases on cooling, consistent with dominant antiferromagnetic interactions and/or thermal depopulation of Dy Stark sublevels. Ac data show frequency-dependent χ′ and χ″ below 10 K without maxima, consistent with SMM behaviour and a blocking temperature below 1.8 K with fast zero-field QTM. Applied small dc fields still leave relaxation outside the 1.8 K experimental window, so no energy barrier or τ0 could be extracted. χ′:χ″ intensity ratio about 4:1.

property_summary: Complex 1 is a Dy4 SMM with two slow magnetic relaxation processes under zero dc field, assigned to the two inequivalent Dy sites. χmT at 300 K is 56.84 cm3 K mol−1 (expected 56.68). ligand_basis: reagent role contains ligand; empty is not evidence of absence
time: reflux 24 h; crystallization about five days
vessel_or_method: reflux in toluene followed by recrystallization from mixed solvent
synthesis_procedure: H4L1 (0.15 g, 0.20 mmol) and Dy(acac)3·2H2O (0.50 g, 1.00 mmol) were dissolved in toluene (4 mL), refluxed for 24 h, and cooled to room temperature. The filtered solid was dissolved in 6 mL CH2Cl2/CH3OH (1:1 v/v) and left about five days at room temperature to give colorless block-shaped crystals.
workup_and_crystallization: filter resulting solid; dissolve in 6 mL CH2Cl2/CH3OH (1:1 v/v); slow evaporation at room temperature yields colorless block crystals
property_summary: χMT at 300 K is 71.42 cm3 K mol−1 (five uncoupled DyIII). χMT falls to 23.43 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, consistent with thermal depopulation and weak antiferromagnetic coupling. Magnetization at 1.9 K/70 kOe is 27.84 Nβ without saturation. Zero-field ac data (1–999 Hz) show χ″ tails typical of SMM-like slow relaxation, but no χ″ maxima, so Ueff cannot be extracted; a 1000 Oe dc field does not produce peaks down to 1.9 K, attributed to fast zero-field relaxation.

title: Pentanuclear [2.2] spirocyclic lanthanide(III) complexes: slow magnetic relaxation of the DyIII analogue

synthesis_procedure: LH3 (0.04 g, 0.18 mmol) was dissolved in 40 mL methanol. Under stirring, DyCl3·6H2O (0.087 g, 0.23 mmol) was added and the mixture was stirred for 20 min at room temperature. synthesis_procedure: All syntheses were performed under aerobic conditions. Slow relaxation attributed mainly to single Dy3+ ions.

time: 1.0 h reflux of silanolate, then 3 h reflux after salt addition; crystallization over a few days
vessel_or_method: reflux in ethanol/acetonitrile; filtration; slow evaporation crystallization
synthesis_procedure: Compounds 1–3 were prepared analogously. PhSi(OMe)3 (0.94 mmol) and NaOH (0.94 mmol) were dissolved in 30 mL ethanol and heated to reflux for 1.0 h. A mixture of lanthanide salts (0.47 mmol total) and Et4NCl (0.47 mmol) in 30 mL MeCN was then added at once. The mixture was refluxed for 3 h, filtered from insoluble residue, and crystalline material was obtained by slow solvent evaporation over a few days. Single crystals were collected; products were dried in vacuum for elemental analysis and yield. For 1, loadings were PhSi(OMe)3 (0.186 g, 0.94 mmol), NaOH (0.038 g, 0.94 mmol), Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (0.16 g, 0.35 mmol), Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.05 g, 0.12 mmol), Et4NCl (0.08 g, 0.47 mmol).
workup_and_crystallization: filtered from insoluble residue to a colourless solution; crystals grown by slow evaporation; dried in vacuum
property_summary: Field-induced SMM: slow magnetization relaxation under 1000 Oe (QTM suppressed); Δ = 11.3 ± 0.6 cm−1, τ0 = (2.5 ± 0.8)×10−6 s. Room-temperature Eu3+ photoluminescence (main 5D0→7F2 at 612 nm) used for self-referenced LIR thermometry of 5D0→7F4 under 590 and 612 nm excitation (293–373 K); maximum Sr = 1.15% K−1 at 293 K.

synthesis_procedure: One-pot synthesis in which the macrocyclic ligand L forms in situ by [2+2] condensation. 4,6-Dihydrazinopyrimidine (0.1 mmol) was dissolved in ethanol/acetonitrile (5 mL/10 mL). DyBr3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) and 3,3'-(propane-1,3-diylbis(oxy))bis(2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) (0.1 mmol) were added sequentially and the mixture was stirred for 10 min. Triethylamine (0.15 mmol) was then added and stirring continued for 6 h. The main text only names the same reagents and slow evaporation, without quantities.

yield: 21.1 mg (21.5% based on the metal salt)
property_summary: Complex 1 is an SMM with two closely spaced relaxation processes and a diamagnetic ground state assigned to toroidal arrangement of Dy(III) moments (SMT). χMT falls from 83.36 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature to 16.36 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with antiferromagnetic interactions. Magnetization at 1.9 K shows an inflection near 10 kOe and does not saturate (34.90 μB at 70 kOe). Arrhenius barriers are 18.04 K (fast) and 15.51 K (slow). Ab initio results indicate nearly axial ground Kramers doublets, in-plane circular anisotropy, antiferromagnetic exchange within each Dy3 triangle and ferromagnetic coupling between the triangles; the exchange-doublet span (10.4 cm−1) is close to the experimental barrier.

synthesis_procedure: DyCl3·6H2O (0.037 g), 2,2'-Hbpt (0.023 g) and NaN3 (0.010 g) were mixed and dissolved in 8 mL analytical-grade methanol, sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, held at 160 °C for 72 h, then cooled to room temperature to give colorless transparent block crystals. Yield about 10% based on Dy.
workup_and_crystallization: cooled to room temperature; colorless transparent block crystals
property_summary: Octanuclear Dy cluster SMM. χMT = 107.8 cm3·K·mol−1 at 300 K (500 Oe), falling to 32.8 cm3·K·mol−1 at 2.0 K. Magnetization 40.81 Nβ at 1.8 K. Zero-dc-field ac susceptibility is frequency-dependent with χM″ maxima above 1.8 K. Arrhenius fit of the first four ln(τ/s) vs 1/T points: Ueff = 9.83(9) K, τ0 = 1.63(2)×10−5 s. Cole–Cole α = 0.33–0.47; Mydosh parameter φ = 0.53–0.59, inconsistent with spin-glass behavior.

title: Synthesis, Structures and Single-Molecule Magnet Behaviour of Octanuclear and Decanuclear Dysprosium Clusters Based on [Dy4(μ4-O)] Tetrahedral Subunits
ligand_basis: reagent role contains ligand; empty is not evidence of absence
vessel_or_method: solvothermal; 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave
synthesis_procedure: Dy(OAc)3·10H2O (0.085 g) and 2,2'-Hbpt (0.023 g) were dissolved in 8 mL analytical-grade methanol, sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, held at 160 °C for 72 h (same conditions as complex 1), then cooled to room temperature to give colorless transparent block crystals. Yield about 37% based on Dy.
workup_and_crystallization: cooled to room temperature; colorless transparent block crystals
property_summary: Decanuclear Dy cluster SMM, described as the highest-nuclearity pure lanthanide SMM under zero dc field in this work. χMT = 133.6 cm3·K·mol−1 at 300 K (500 Oe), falling sharply below ~45 K to 61.2 cm3·K·mol−1 at 2.0 K. Magnetization 51.62 Nβ at 1.8 K. Zero-dc-field ac susceptibility is frequency-dependent with χM″ peaks above 1.8 K. Arrhenius: Ueff = 12.05(2) K, τ0 = 6.75(8)×10−7 s. Cole–Cole α = 0.33–0.39; φ = 0.35–0.56.
